docs/docker.md lists official images ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:{full,light,server}, and -cuda ('compiled with CUDA 12 support'), -cuda13 ('CUDA 13'), -rocm, -musa, -intel, -vulkan, -openvino, -s390x variants; 'full' includes llama-cli/llama-completion and conversion tools, 'light' only llama-cli/llama-completion, 'server' only llama-server; 'The GPU enabled images are not currently tested by CI beyond being built'. docker.yml builds the cuda/cuda12 tags with cuda_version 12.8.1 and cuda13 with 13.3.0, each for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

.devops/cuda.Dockerfile: ARG CUDA_VERSION=12.8.1, UBUNTU_VERSION=24.04, base docker.io/nvidia/cuda:${CUDA_VERSION}-{devel,runtime}-ubuntu${UBUNTU_VERSION}; build line is 'cmake -B build -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=ON -DGGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF ${CMAKE_ARGS} -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-Wl,--allow-shlib-undefined .' where CMAKE_ARGS is only set to -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES when CUDA_DOCKER_ARCH != default — i.e. GGML_RPC is never enabled (ggml/CMakeLists.txt: option(GGML_RPC 'ggml: use RPC' OFF). 'light' copies llama, llama-cli, llama-completion; 'server' copies llama, llama-server; 'full' copies build/bin/*. Hence no official image ships ggml-rpc-server or the RPC backend (inferred from the Dockerfile; image contents not pulled).

tools/rpc/README.md: 'This example and the RPC backend are currently in a proof-of-concept development stage. As such, the functionality is fragile and insecure. Never run the RPC server on an open network or in a sensitive environment!' Build: 'On each remote host, build the backends for each accelerator by adding -DGGML_RPC=ON' e.g. 'cmake .. -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON'; 'On the main host build llama.cpp with the backends for the local devices and add -DGGML_RPC=ON'; usage 'llama-cli -hf ggml-org/gemma-3-1b-it-GGUF -ngl 99 --rpc 192.168.88.10:50052,192.168.88.11:50052'. 'By default, ggml-rpc-server exposes all available accelerator devices on the host. If there are no accelerators, it exposes a single CPU device.' Device selection via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or --device. Cache: '-c' ... 'stored in the $HOME/.cache/llama.cpp/rpc directory and can be controlled via the LLAMA_CACHE environment variable'. Debug: GGML_RPC_DEBUG=1. RDMA auto-negotiated when libibverbs found at build time. The executable target is ggml-rpc-server (tools/rpc/CMakeLists.txt set(TARGET ggml-rpc-server)). docs/build.md contains no RPC section.

tools/rpc/rpc-server.cpp usage at this tag: '-h, --help', '-t, --threads N  number of threads for the CPU device (default: hardware_concurrency()/2, min 1)', '-d, --device <dev1,dev2,...>  comma-separated list of devices', '-H, --host HOST  host to bind to (default: 127.0.0.1)', '-p, --port PORT  port to bind to (default: 50052)', '-c, --cache  enable local file cache'. There is no -m/--mem option. If host != 127.0.0.1 it prints: 'WARNING: Host ('%s') is != '127.0.0.1' / Never expose the RPC server to an open network! / This is an experimental feature and is not secure!'. With -c the cache dir is fs_get_cache_directory()+'rpc/' where the base is $LLAMA_CACHE, else $XDG_CACHE_HOME/llama.cpp or $HOME/.cache/llama.cpp (Linux), ~/Library/Caches/llama.cpp (macOS), %LOCALAPPDATA%/llama.cpp (Windows). Startup prints each device as '<name>: <description> (<total> MiB, <free> MiB free)'.

ggml/src/ggml-rpc/transport.cpp: the server socket is AF_INET with SO_REUSEADDR, binds to inet_addr(host) and rejects non-dotted-quad hosts ('Invalid host address'); the client resolves the --rpc host with gethostbyname() and connects with plain TCP (TCP_NODELAY). No TLS, authentication, or proxy support exists in the transport. ggml/include/ggml-rpc.h defines RPC_PROTO_MAJOR_VERSION 5, MINOR 1, PATCH 0 and GGML_RPC_MAX_SERVERS 16; ggml-rpc.cpp rejects a server when 'response.major != RPC_PROTO_MAJOR_VERSION || response.minor > RPC_PROTO_MINOR_VERSION' with 'RPC server version mismatch'. Client-side devices are named 'RPC<idx>[<endpoint>]'.

common/arg.cpp: '--rpc SERVERS  comma-separated list of RPC servers (host:port)' (env LLAMA_ARG_RPC); add_rpc_devices() calls ggml_backend_load_all(), looks up backend 'RPC' (throws 'failed to find RPC backend' if the build lacks GGML_RPC), and calls ggml_backend_rpc_add_server(endpoint) + ggml_backend_register for each endpoint. '-ngl N  max. number of layers to store in VRAM, either an exact number, auto, or all (default: auto)'; common.h n_gpu_layers=-1 (auto) and fit_params=true ('whether to fit unset model/context parameters to free device memory'). '-sm {none,layer,row,tensor}' with 'layer (default): split layers and KV across GPUs (pipelined)'; '-ts N0,N1,...  fraction of the model to offload to each GPU, comma-separated list of proportions, e.g. 3,1'; '-dev <dev1,dev2,..>  comma-separated list of devices to use for offloading (none = don't offload)'; '--list-devices  print list of available devices and exit'; '-mg INDEX'.

Layer split semantics: tools/rpc/README.md: 'By default, llama.cpp distributes model weights and the KV cache across all available devices -- both local and remote -- in proportion to each device's available memory. You can override this behavior with the --tensor-split option'. src/llama-model.cpp implements this: when tensor_split is all zeros, '// default split, by free memory' — splits[i] = free bytes from ggml_backend_dev_memory(dev,&free,&total) (falling back to host memory if a device reports 0/0); layers are then assigned by upper_bound over the normalised cumulative splits, and the input layer is always kept on the CPU.

tools/server/README.md option table: '--rpc SERVERS  comma-separated list of RPC servers (host:port) (env: LLAMA_ARG_RPC)'; '--log-disable  Log disable'; '--log-file FNAME  Log to file (env: LLAMA_ARG_LOG_FILE)'; '-v, --verbose, --log-verbose  Set verbosity level to infinity'; '-lv, --verbosity, --log-verbosity N  ... 0: generic output, 1: error, 2: warning, 3: info, 4: trace, 5: debug (default: 3) (env: LLAMA_ARG_LOG_VERBOSITY)'; '--metrics ... (default: disabled)'; '--props  enable changing global properties via POST /props (default: disabled)'; '--slots, --no-slots  expose slots monitoring endpoint (default: enabled)'; '--slot-save-path PATH  path to save slot kv cache (default: disabled)'. llama-server defaults --host 127.0.0.1, --port 8080 (common.h hostname/port; env LLAMA_ARG_HOST/LLAMA_ARG_PORT).

Prompt/request logging in llama-server is debug-level only: tools/server/server-http.cpp logs SRV_DBG("request:  %s", req.body) and SRV_DBG("response: %s", res.body); per-token prompt dumps are SLT_DBG. SRV_DBG/SLT_DBG map to LOG_DBG = LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG (5) in common/log.h, above the default threshold 3, so at default verbosity request bodies are not logged; -v (INT_MAX) logs them. common/arg.cpp also has '--log-prompts-dir PATH  Log prompts to directory (auto-created if not present; only used for debugging, default: disabled)' for SERVER and CLI, and '--log-disable' pauses the main log entirely. '--verbose-prompt' exists but is not registered for the server example.

tools/llama-bench/README.md usage lists '-rpc, --rpc <rpc_servers>  register RPC devices (comma separated)', alongside '-ngl, --n-gpu-layers <n> (default: -1)', '-sm, --split-mode <none|layer|row|tensor> (default: layer)', '-mg, --main-gpu <i> (default: 0)', '-ts, --tensor-split <ts0/ts1/..> (default: 0)', '-dev, --device <dev0/dev1/...> (default: auto)'.

For a build covering all CUDA GPUs, disable GGML_NATIVE: cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF'; to pin: 'cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="86;89"'; to pick a toolkit: 'cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/opt/cuda-11.7/bin/nvcc -DCMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH="/opt/cuda-11.7/lib64;\$ORIGIN" -DCMAKE_BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH=ON'. facts.statement: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18) 'for CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES'; find_package(CUDAToolkit) with message(FATAL_ERROR "CUDA Toolkit not found") otherwise. If CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES is unset: GGML_NATIVE with CUDA>=11.6 and CMake>=3.24 => 'native'; else list = [50-virtual 61-virtual 70-virtual only if CUDAToolkit_VERSION < 13] + 75-virtual 80-virtual 86-real + [89-real 90-virtual if >=11.8] + [120a-real if >=12.8] + [121a-real if >=12.9]. Comment: '50 == Maxwell, lowest CUDA 12 standard ... XX-virtual == compile CUDA code as PTX, do JIT compilation to binary code on first run; XX-real == compile CUDA code as device code for this specific architecture'. No minimum CUDA toolkit version is enforced; common.cuh gates features on CUDART_VERSION >= 11070 / 11080 / 12000 / 12030.

Maxwell (cc 5.2) code-path limits in llama.cpp CUDA: common.cuh defines GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL 600, GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A 610 '// minimum compute capability for __dp4a, an intrinsic for byte-wise dot products', VOLTA 700, TURING 750, AMPERE 800; mmq.cu returns false (MMQ not used) when ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) < GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A; ggml-cuda.cu disables mul_mat_vec fusion when cc <= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL ('fusion is not universally faster on Pascal'). No code path refuses cc 5.x outright; a GTX 970 runs through the generic/cuBLAS paths.

CUDA 12.9 release notes, 1.5.2 Deprecated Architectures: 'Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta architectures are now feature-complete with no further enhancements planned. While CUDA Toolkit 12.x series will continue to support building applications for these architectures, offline compilation and library support will be removed in the next major CUDA Toolkit version release.' CUDA 12.9 GA toolkit driver >=575.51.03; 12.9 Update 1 >=575.57.08.

CUDA 13.0 release notes, 2.6.2 Deprecated Architectures: 'Architecture support for Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta is considered feature-complete. Offline compilation and library support for these architectures have been removed in CUDA Toolkit 13.0 major version release. The use of CUDA Toolkits through the 12.x series to build applications for these architectures will continue to be supported, but newer toolkits will be unable to target these architectures.' cuFFT: 'Removed support for Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta GPUs, corresponding to compute capabilities earlier than Turing.' CUDA 13.0 GA Linux driver >=580.65.06; '13.x series are ABI-compatible with drivers ... r580 and newer'.

CUDA 12.2 release notes: Table 3 'CUDA 12.2 GA — Linux x86_64 Driver Version >=535.54.03'; Table 2 minimum driver for CUDA minor version compatibility: CUDA 12.2.x/12.1.x/12.0.x >=525.60.13. (Driver 535 on the hub is the 12.2 GA toolkit driver.)

CUDA Compatibility guide, Minor Version Compatibility caveats: 'Applications using PTX will see runtime issues — Applications that compile device code to PTX will not work on older drivers. If the application requires PTX then administrators have to upgrade the installed driver.' and 'Requires target architecture argument to NVCC — Minor Compatibility requires passing the target architecture argument to NVCC, for example nvcc -arch=sm_xx.' Also 'features introduced in a newer version of the toolkit and driver may return ... cudaErrorCallRequiresNewerDriver'. Forward Compatibility page: 'Forward Compatibility is applicable only for systems with: NVIDIA Data Center GPUs. Select NGC Server Ready SKUs of RTX cards. Jetson boards.'

Derived constraint for the hub (GTX 970, cc 5.2, driver 535 = CUDA 12.2 GA driver): llama.cpp's default Maxwell target is '50-virtual' (PTX, JIT at runtime) and NVIDIA says PTX built with a newer 12.x toolkit will not run on an older driver under minor-version compatibility; therefore on the hub either build with the CUDA 12.2 toolkit, or build with any 12.x toolkit and pass -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=52-real (SASS for sm_52, which minor-version compatibility does support on driver >=525.60.13). CUDA 13.x cannot target cc 5.2 and needs driver >=580 anyway. This combination of F17+F21+F23 is an inference; the 'build with 12.2 on driver 535' path has not yet been executed on the hub.

NVIDIA driver 535 README FAQ 'How and when are the NVIDIA device files created?': device files are created by the user-space driver component or, lacking root, by 'the setuid root nvidia-modprobe utility'; 'it will default to creating the device files with the following attributes: UID: 0 - root, GID: 0 - root, Mode: 0666 - rw-rw-rw-. Existing device files are changed if their attributes don't match these defaults.' Different attributes can be set with kernel module parameters NVreg_DeviceFileUID, NVreg_DeviceFileGID, NVreg_DeviceFileMode (example: UID=0, GID=44 (video), Mode=0660); 'The NVreg_ModifyDeviceFiles NVIDIA kernel module parameter will disable dynamic device file management, if set to 0.' 'When possible, it is recommended to use your Linux distribution's native mechanisms for managing kernel module loading and device file creation.'
facts.version: NVIDIA Linux driver 535.261.03 README (identical text in 535.247.01 and 535.230.02)

systemd loginctl(1): 'enable-linger [USER…], disable-linger [USER…] — Enable/disable user lingering for one or more users. If enabled for a specific user, a user manager is spawned for the user at boot and kept around after logouts. This allows users who are not logged in to run long-running services. Takes one or more user names or numeric UIDs as argument. If no argument is specified, enables/disables lingering for the user of the session of the caller. See also KillUserProcesses= setting in logind.conf(5). Added in version 233.'

Tailscale KB 'Userspace networking mode (for containers)' (last validated Nov 12, 2025): 'Tailscale works on Linux systems using a device driver called /dev/net/tun ... For those environments [without it], userspace networking mode offers a different way of running, where tailscaled functions as a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy which other processes in the container can connect through.' Enabled with 'tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking --socks5-server=localhost:1055 --outbound-http-proxy-listen=localhost:1055' or FLAGS="--tun=userspace-networking" in /etc/default/tailscaled; 'After Tailscale is authenticated, your application can connect using a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy or both ... generally by setting the ALL_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY environment variables'; 'Userspace networking mode is primarily for serverless environments.' The page does not describe how inbound connections reach local services in this mode.

Derived: because ggml-rpc/llama-server use direct TCP connect()/bind() with no proxy support (F10) and Tailscale userspace mode only exposes tailnet connectivity through a local SOCKS5/HTTP proxy (F29), the hub as currently configured cannot act as the --rpc client to workers' tailnet IPs nor bind llama-server/ggml-rpc-server to a tailnet IPv4 address. Whether 'tailscale serve' could front an inbound TCP port in userspace mode was not verified from Tailscale docs in this dossier.

llama.cpp LICENSE: 'MIT License — Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors'. Version metadata at v0.2.0/b10581: CMakeLists LLAMA_VERSION 0.2.0, ggml 0.21.0 (shipped as libllama.so.0.2.0 and libggml-base.so.0.21.0). The RPC backend was added by PR #6829 'ggml : add RPC backend' by rgerganov (Radoslav Gerganov), merged 2024-05-14; CODEOWNERS assigns /ggml/src/ggml-rpc/ and /tools/rpc/ to @ggml-org/ggml-rpc ('ggml-org/ggml-rpc : rgerganov').

recommendations: Pin llama.cpp to a single tag for the whole fleet and record it in the spec as 'v0.2.0 (= b10566)'; RPC protocol 5.1.0 mismatch across builds is a hard failure, so every node's ggml-rpc-server and the hub's llama-server must come from the same tag (F1, F10).

Linux CUDA nodes must build from source: cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON (add -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF or an explicit CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES when building on one box for another). Do not plan on the official Docker images or the ubuntu release tarballs for GPU RPC workers — the tarballs are CPU/Vulkan only and the images lack the RPC backend (F3, F4, F7). The CPU/Vulkan tarballs are still useful for a quick no-GPU smoke test (they do contain ggml-rpc-server).

Hub (GTX 970, driver 535): build with the CUDA 12.2 toolkit that matches driver 535, or with any 12.x toolkit plus -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=52-real so Maxwell gets SASS rather than PTX (F17, F21, F23, F24). Never install CUDA 13 on that box for this purpose (needs driver >=580 and cannot target cc 5.2). Treat the 970 as a 'fits, but slow' device (no MMQ/dp4a, F18) — primarily extra VRAM for the split, and consider the Vulkan backend as a fallback experiment if the CUDA 12.2 build fights the host toolchain.

RTX 3050 node on CUDA 13.1: default arch list covers 86-real; requires driver >=590.44.01 (F22). RTX 2070 Super (cc 7.5) is covered by every default list. Keep per-node builds native (GGML_NATIVE on) since each node compiles its own ggml-rpc-server.

Write the rpc-server unit as: ExecStart=.../ggml-rpc-server -H <node's Tailscale IPv4> -p 50052 [-c] [-d CUDA0]; -H must be a dotted IPv4 literal (F10) and the upstream 'not secure' banner will print and is expected (F9). Add the spec sentence that the RPC server is unauthenticated raw TCP and the tailnet is the only boundary; combine with Tailscale ACLs limiting port 50052 to the hub.

Resolve the hub's Tailscale userspace-mode problem before Phase 1 (F29, F30): either switch solarplexus to kernel/tun mode, or run llama-server on a tun-mode node and keep the hub as a worker only after confirming it can accept inbound tailnet TCP. This is an ADR-worthy decision (topology ADR 0006 is reserved).

llama-server on the hub: --host <tailnet IPv4> --port 8080 --rpc <worker1>:50052,<worker2>:50052 -ngl auto (default) and let the default free-memory split do the work; only add -ts if the split is bad. Use --list-devices first to confirm RPC<n>[host:port] devices appear (F11, F12). Keep logging at default -lv 3 and never use -v or --log-prompts-dir in service units (F14); consider --no-slots and leave --metrics/--props off unless needed; optionally --log-file to a member-readable location for the thank-you board.
Benchmark the split with llama-bench --rpc <servers> -ngl 99 before committing to a model, since RPC exists to fit, not to speed up (F15).

Service user: run ggml-rpc-server as a dedicated non-root user under a user manager with loginctl enable-linger and the unit in ~/.config/systemd/user (F27, F28); verify ls -l /dev/nvidia* shows 0666 (F25) and, if a distro has tightened it, add the user to the group named by the device GID rather than changing module parameters. Set LLAMA_CACHE (or let it default to ~/.cache/llama.cpp/rpc) to a disk with room for the cached tensors when using -c.
Credit rows: llama.cpp row already exists; add the release/tag convention and the RPC maintainer handle (rgerganov) to docs, and add Tailscale userspace-mode note to the hub's page.
open_questions: Does the hub really need Tailscale in userspace mode (no /dev/net/tun)? If the reason is historical, moving to tun mode removes the blocker in F30; if it is a hard constraint, does 'tailscale serve --tcp' accept inbound RPC and can the hub reach workers at all as an RPC client? Not verified from Tailscale docs here.

Can the CUDA 12.2 toolkit be installed alongside the hub's current OS toolchain (gcc/glibc compatibility), or is the simpler route -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=52-real with a newer 12.x toolkit? Needs a spike on solarplexus (F24 is an inference until executed).
Is the GTX 970's 4 GB worth the RPC round-trips for the chosen Phase 1 model, or should the hub be the llama-server host with the 2070 Super and 3050 as RPC workers? llama-bench numbers needed.

What exactly is in the CUDA 12.4 Windows release zip beyond ggml-cuda.dll (we observed ggml-rpc-server.exe and CPU dlls in it), and is the cudart zip required on a friend's Windows PC that lacks a CUDA toolkit? Needs a Windows test before the Windows onboarding card is written.
Does the macOS release tarball's ggml-rpc-server work unsigned on a friend's Mac (Gatekeeper), or must Macs build from source / use brew? Not researched in this dossier.
Will the v0.x stable cadence be slow enough to pin for a whole phase, or should the spec pin the b-number directly (v0.2.0 = b10566)?
Distro-specific /dev/nvidia* permissions on Ubuntu Server (hub) and Arch/EndeavourOS (laptops): confirm with ls -l on each node; the NVIDIA default is 0666 but udev rules can differ.

verdicts.reason: Verified against the cited primary source (GitHub release page, fetched) and the GitHub REST API for ggml-org/llama.cpp (via authenticated gh). All load-bearing facts hold as of 2026-08-22: (1) GET /releases/latest returns tag v0.2.0, prerelease=false, draft=false, published_at 2026-08-21T18:32:48Z (exact match); among the newest 100 releases no non-prerelease has a later published_at (newest releases b10567–b10581 are all prerelease=true), and the only v0.x tags are v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.2, v0.2.0. (2) refs/tags/v0.2.0 is an annotated tag object 8a35040e whose target commit is bb4caa7540188872173c44d161602d9271386413 ("llama.cpp : bump version to 0.2.0 (#27498)"); refs/tags/b10566 is a lightweight tag pointing to the same commit bb4caa75. (3) The release body contains verbatim "tag `vX.Y.Z` - stable, slower release cadence, recommended for downstream distribution and casual users" and "tag `b[NUM]` - bleeding edge, faster release cadence, recommended for developers and technical users" and links "Nightly build: b10566". (4) The release's only uploaded asset is nightly-tag.txt (7 bytes), whose content is "b10566\n". (5) The b10566 release (prerelease=true, published 2026-08-21T18:25:36Z, target bb4caa75) carries 26 assets including llama-b10566-bin-macos-arm64/x64, ubuntu, win-cuda etc. Two non-refuting nuances: the claim's quotation truncates the b[NUM] bullet before "recommended for developers and technical users" (elision, not misquote); and the HTML page shows "3 assets" because GitHub adds auto-generated Source code (zip/tar.gz) archives — the API lists a single uploaded asset, consistent with the claim. Note also the release's target_commitish is 5a32f7b6 (master head when the release was created), but the tag itself resolves to bb4caa75 as claimed.

Verified against the cited primary source (the GitHub release page HTML for tag b10581) and the GitHub REST API (repos/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tags/b10581, fetched 2026-08-22 12:36 UTC via authenticated gh). API fields match the claim exactly: tag_name=b10581, prerelease=true, draft=false, published_at=2026-08-22T10:13:08Z, target_commitish=2115b73d8ebdbd659075cce66c609506863bc826, 26 assets. The asset list on both the HTML page and the API is byte-for-byte the 26 names in the claim (3 cudart-win-cuda zips; 11 ubuntu/macos/android tar.gz incl. ubuntu-x64, ubuntu-arm64, ubuntu-s390x, ubuntu-vulkan-{x64,arm64}, ubuntu-sycl-{fp16,fp32}-x64, ubuntu-openvino-2026.3-x64; 10 win zips incl. cuda-12.4-x64, cuda-13.3-x64, cuda-13.4-arm64, rocm-7.14-x64, vulkan-x64, sycl-x64, openvino-2026.3-x64, opencl-adreno-arm64, cpu-x64, cpu-arm64; ui.tar.gz; xcframework.zip). No asset name contains 'ubuntu-cuda', 'ubuntu-rocm', 'linux-cuda' or 'linux-rocm', so 'no Linux CUDA and no Linux ROCm asset' holds. The releases list (per_page=5) confirms b10581 is still the newest release as of check time (b10580, b10578, b10577, b10576 precede it, all published 2026-08-22). Only nuance, not a refutation: GitHub's /releases/latest endpoint (non-prerelease) points at v0.2.0 (2026-08-21), which is consistent with the claim's explicit qualifier 'nightly ... prerelease=true'.

Fetched the primary source (raw release.yml at tag b10581, 1779 lines; also b10566 for comparison). Most of the claim is verified verbatim: line 33 sets env CMAKE_ARGS exactly as quoted; ubuntu-cpu (lines 169-255) builds with -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=ON -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON ... ${{ env.CMAKE_ARGS }} and tars `-C ./build/bin .` into llama-<tag>-bin-ubuntu-<x64|arm64|s390x>.tar.gz; windows-cuda (lines 980-1085) is the only CUDA job (matrix cuda 12.4/x64, 13.3/x64, 13.4/arm64) built with -DGGML_CPU=OFF -DGGML_CUDA=ON (plus -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=ON -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_BORINGSSL=ON, --target ggml-cuda only). However, the claim that ${{ env.CMAKE_ARGS }} is passed to the "sycl jobs" is NOT supported: grep shows exactly 7 live references to ${{ env.CMAKE_ARGS }} (lines 145 macos-cpu, 231 ubuntu-cpu, 318 ubuntu-vulkan, 411 android-arm64, 512 ubuntu-24-openvino, 636 windows-openvino, 733 windows-cpu). windows-sycl (lines 1132-1143) builds with `-DGGML_BACKEND_DL=ON -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DGGML_CPU=OFF -DGGML_SYCL=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_BORINGSSL=ON` and --target ggml-sycl, no CMAKE_ARGS; ubuntu-24-sycl (lines 1251-1268) builds with `-DGGML_SYCL=ON ... -DLLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_SYCL_F16=...`, no CMAKE_ARGS (so GGML_RPC is left at its CMake default there). The only other occurrence (line 1380) is inside a fully commented-out ubuntu-rocm job. Same is true at b10566 (identical CMAKE_ARGS reference lines). So the job list in the claim is wrong on one element; strict standard => refuted.

Every element of the claim matches verbatim: line 1 `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18)  # for CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`; line 3 `find_package(CUDAToolkit)` with final `else() message(FATAL_ERROR "CUDA Toolkit not found")` (line 268); inside `if (NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)`: `GGML_NATIVE AND CUDAToolkit_VERSION >= "11.6" AND CMAKE_VERSION >= "3.24"` => "native", else `50-virtual 61-virtual 70-virtual` only if `CUDAToolkit_VERSION VERSION_LESS "13"`, then `75-virtual 80-virtual 86-real`, then `89-real 90-virtual` if >= 11.8, `120a-real` if >= 12.8, `121a-real` if >= 12.9. Quoted comments ("50 == Maxwell, lowest CUDA 12 standard", "XX-virtual == compile CUDA code as PTX, do JIT compilation to binary code on first run", "XX-real == compile CUDA code as device code for this specific architecture") are exact. The only FATAL_ERROR in the file is the not-found case; there is no minimum-CUDA-version check (only VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL feature gates at 10.1/11.6/11.8/12.8/12.9), so "no minimum CUDA toolkit version is enforced" holds. common.cuh at b10581 does gate on CUDART_VERSION >= 11070 (GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB; also CUDART_HMAX=11070), >= 11080 and >= 12030 (GGML_CUDA_USE_PDL, MSVC-dependent), >= 12000 (cublasGetStatusString; CUDART_HMASK=12000). Minor incompleteness only, not a falsity: common.cuh also has gates at >= 11010 (GGML_CUDA_ASSUME) and >= 12080 (e8m0->bf16 intrinsic); the claim's list is non-exhaustive but every value it names is real. Source is the primary upstream file; claim is current for the stated version.

Verified against the raw files at the exact tag b10581 (raw.githubusercontent.com, all HTTP 200; the cited blob URL also resolves 200). common.cuh lines 50-54 read verbatim: `#define GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL 600`, `#define GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A 610 // minimum compute capability for __dp4a, an intrinsic for byte-wise dot products`, `VOLTA 700`, `TURING 750`, `AMPERE 800`. mmq.cu line 316 (inside ggml_cuda_should_use_mmq): `if (ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) < GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A) { return false; }`. ggml-cuda.cu lines 1798-1802 (inside ggml_cuda_should_fuse_mul_mat_vec_q): `// fusion is not universally faster on Pascal` / `if (cc <= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL) { return false; }`. No outright refusal of cc 5.x found: ggml_cuda_init only logs "compute capability %d.%d" (no abort); ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch returns -1 rather than aborting when no compiled arch <= cc; supports_op has no low-cc rejection; CUDA graphs are merely disabled below Volta (debug log); flash-attn falls back to tile/vec kernels when no tensor cores. Dispatcher (ggml-cuda.cu 1815-1868) for cc 5.2 on quantized weights: MMVQ for small batches (with the software dp4a fallback in common.cuh 735-738, `#if __CUDA_ARCH__ >= GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A ... #else` byte-wise emulation), then cuBLAS since MMQ is off — consistent with "generic/cuBLAS paths". Minor caveats, not refutations: (1) the fusion gate is specifically for mul_mat_vec_q fusion; (2) ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt at b10581 only adds 50-virtual/61-virtual/70-virtual when CUDAToolkit_VERSION < 13 (comment: "50 == Maxwell, lowest CUDA 12 standard"), so a GTX 970 requires a CUDA 12.x toolchain build — a toolchain/build-config limit, not an llama.cpp code-path refusal.

Cited source fetched (HTTP 200, primary NVIDIA archive). It supports most of the claim verbatim: section 1.5.2 "Deprecated Architectures" exists on the 12.9.0 page and the Maxwell/Pascal/Volta quote matches word-for-word; Table 3 lists "CUDA 12.9 GA | >=575.51.03 (Linux x86_64) | >=576.02 (Windows)". However the claim's final clause "12.9 Update 1 >=575.57.08" does NOT appear anywhere on the cited 12.9.0 page (string absent; Table 3 there tops out at 12.9 GA). That figure is only on the separate 12.9.1 archive page (Table 3: "CUDA 12.9 Update 1 | >=575.57.08 | >=576.57"), where the deprecation section is numbered 2.6.1.1, not 1.5.2. Additionally, a CUDA 12.9 Update 2 exists (archive 12.9.2; Table 3: "CUDA 12.9 Update 2 | >=575.57.08 | >=576.57", same deprecation text at 2.6.1.1) which the claim omits. Numbers are all accurate; the defect is that the claim as stated is not fully supported by its single cited URL and is incomplete for the 12.9 series. Strict reading => refuted on citation coverage, not on substance.

(1) Section "2.6.2. Deprecated Architectures" reads exactly: "Architecture support for Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta is considered feature-complete. Offline compilation and library support for these architectures have been removed in CUDA Toolkit 13.0 major version release. The use of CUDA Toolkits through the 12.x series to build applications for these architectures will continue to be supported, but newer toolkits will be unable to target these architectures." (2) cuFFT 13.0 "Deprecations" reads exactly: "Removed support for Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta GPUs, corresponding to compute capabilities earlier than Turing." (3) Table "CUDA Toolkit and Corresponding Driver Versions" row "CUDA 13.0 GA" lists Linux x86_64 Driver Version ">=580.65.06" (Windows column is N/A, and the component table lists NVIDIA Linux Driver 580.65.06). (4) Section 2.3 reads: "CUDA Toolkit releases in the 13.x series are ABI-compatible with drivers corresponding to the same series (r580 and newer)." — the claim's ellipsized quote is a faithful abridgement. # DOSSIER R04 — Model selection for Phase 1 (CORVID)
Date verified: 2026-08-22. Fleet assumption (from task): largest single node = 6 GB VRAM + ~19 GB free RAM ≈ 25 GB; pool ≈ 18 GB VRAM (8+4+6) + ≈63 GB RAM ≈ 81 GB. llama.cpp pinned reference: stable tag v0.2.0 (2026-08-21) / nightly b10581 (2026-08-22).

## 1. Ranking basis (named, dated)
- **Primary basis: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1.1** (9 evals: GDPval-AA v2, tau3-Banking, Terminal-Bench v2.1, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, HLE, GPQA Diamond, CritPt), open-weights table and per-model pages as displayed 2026-08-22 (R04-F1..F10). Scores are only comparable within this index version; they are NOT comparable to 2025-era AA numbers.
- **Cross-check: Arena (ex-LMArena) text leaderboard, snapshot "Last updated Aug 21, 2026", 7.9M votes / 394 models** (R04-F11): every open-weight entry in the top 50 is frontier-scale (GLM-5.x, Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiMo-V2.5-Pro) — nothing that fits an 81 GB pool. So Arena tells us the ceiling, AA tells us the best-per-GB.
- **Demand signal: Hugging Face GGUF trending (2026-08-22)** is dominated by Qwen3.8-27B quants (unsloth repo 6.32M downloads) plus Muse-Glimmer-30B and Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B (R04-F12).
- Not used: HF Open LLM Leaderboard (no usable 2026 table surfaced; see open questions).

## 2. KV-cache arithmetic method (llama.cpp)
Per llama.cpp `llama-hparams.cpp` (R04-F45): per layer, K row width = n_embd_head_k × n_head_kv and V row width = n_embd_head_v × n_head_kv; the server's K/V cache types default to f16 = 2 bytes (R04-F44). So **KV bytes/token = Σ_layers 2 × n_head_kv × head_dim × 2 B** over full-attention layers; sliding-window layers are capped at the window length; linear-attention (Gated DeltaNet) layers hold a constant per-sequence recurrent state instead of a growing KV. All KV numbers below are DERIVED from primary config.json values (marked unverified = computed, not measured). **Critical:** `-c/--ctx-size` defaults to 0 = "loaded from model" (R04-F44), i.e. 262,144 for Qwen3.8-27B and 131,072 for Llama 3.3 70B — always pass `-c 4096`/`-c 8192` explicitly or KV balloons (16 GiB / 40 GiB).

## 3. Candidates that are IMPOSSIBLE on one node (> ~25 GB) yet FIT the pool (< ~81 GB)
Sizes are HF byte counts in decimal GB (1 GB = 1e9 B). KV at f16; totals = weights + KV(8k) (+ recurrent/SWA state where relevant).

## 4. Fallback list (> 8 GB VRAM, i.e. does not fit the laptop's RTX 2070 Super alone; < 25 GB so it fits one node's VRAM+RAM) — proves a 2-GPU split before the 3-node + RAM split
- Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M: ggml-org 18.97 GB / bartowski 17.77 GB / unsloth UD-Q4_K_M 16.46 GB (+0.54 GB KV @8k)
- Gemma 4 31B-it Q4_K_M 18.32 GB (unsloth) / Q4_0 17.99 GB (ggml-org)
- Muse-Glimmer-30B UD-Q4_K_XL 15.88 GB (unsloth) / official KQuant Q4_K_M 16.76 GB
- Qwen3-32B Q4_K_M 19.76 GB; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B Q4_K_M 19.85 GB
- Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507 Q4_K_M 18.56 GB; Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Q4_0 18.90 GB
- Gemma-3-27b-it Q4_K_M 16.55 GB (gated); Mistral-Small-3.2 Q4_K_M 14.33 GB; gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 12.11 GB

## 5. Recommendation (headline)
**Phase-1 demo model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B at Q8_0 from ggml-org/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (28.60 GB, 26.6 GiB), `-c 8192`.** It is the highest-scoring open-weight model in its size class on the named basis (AA v4.1.1 = 52, #1/137), Apache-2.0, ungated, the most-downloaded GGUF on HF this week, and its Q8_0 is the smallest quant that clears the 25 GB line with comfortable margin (≈29.3 GB incl. KV) while needing only ~11 GB of CPU RAM beyond the pool's 18 GB VRAM. Its tiny KV (64 KiB/token, hybrid linear attention) means context size barely moves the arithmetic. Same-class backups: Muse-Glimmer-30B Q8_0 (29.6 GB, AA 35) and Gemma 4 31B Q8_0 (32.6 GB, AA 30), both Apache-2.0. Keep Llama 3.3 70B / DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B as the "classic 70B" fallback only if Qwen3.8's hybrid architecture misbehaves over RPC — they are plain-attention and known-good but gated/heavier (≥27.5 GB at IQ3_XXS, 320 KiB/token KV). Avoid gpt-oss-120b (no headroom) and gated Gemma 3 for v1.

## 6. llama.cpp facts that gate the plan
- RPC README (master, 2026-08-22): "By default, llama.cpp distributes model weights and the KV cache across all available devices -- both local and remote -- in proportion to each device's available memory"; override with `--tensor-split`; build `-DGGML_RPC=ON`; the server binary is now shown as `bin/ggml-rpc-server -p 50052` with `--device CUDA0` and `-c` (local cache); warning: "Never run the RPC server on an open network or in a sensitive environment!" (R04-F42).
- Top-level README now shows `llama cli -hf …` / `llama serve -hf …`, while tools/server/README still shows `./llama-server` (R04-F46/F47) → confirm binary names at the pinned tag before writing setup docs.
- CUDA CMake defaults: compute-capability 50/61/70 targets are added only when CUDA < 13 ("Maxwell, lowest CUDA 12 standard") (R04-F48) → the GTX 970 (sm_52) hub must build with its CUDA 12.2; the RTX 3050 node on CUDA 13.1 cannot produce a 970-capable binary (irrelevant since each node builds its own).
- Server defaults: `--host 127.0.0.1`, `-ctk/-ctv f16`, `-ngl auto`, `-np -1 (auto)`, `--kv-unified` on when slots auto, `-c 0 = loaded from model` (R04-F44).

## 7. Licence summary for §4 rows
Apache-2.0 / ungated: Qwen3.8-27B (Copyright 2026 Alibaba Cloud), Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507, Muse-Glimmer-30B (Meta Superintelligence Lab), Gemma 4 31B (Google; ai.google.dev Gemma 4 licence page = Apache 2.0), Mistral-Small-3.2-24B, gpt-oss-120b/20b. MIT: DeepSeek-R1 distills (70B inherits Llama 3.3 Community Licence per its README). OpenMDW-1.1: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. GATED ("manual" approval on HF): meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (Llama 3.3 Community License, 700M-MAU clause, "Built with Llama" attribution, "Llama" naming) and google/gemma-3-27b-it (Gemma Terms of Use, last modified April 1 2026: Notice file + use-restriction passthrough + Prohibited Use Policy).

llama.cpp docs/build.md ('Build llama.cpp locally', master 2026-08-22) contains no KV-cache sizing notes and no RPC build section; it documents CUDA builds (e.g. cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="86;89") and the tuning options GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ, GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS, GGML_CUDA_PEER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE, GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS, plus Metal and Vulkan sections. KV sizing must therefore be derived from model configs + llama-hparams.cpp (R04-F45).

llama.cpp tools/server/README.md (master 2026-08-22) option defaults: '-c, --ctx-size N: size of the prompt context (default: 0, 0 = loaded from model)'; '-ctk, --cache-type-k TYPE: KV cache data type for K (allowed: f32, f16, bf16, q8_0, q4_0, q4_1, iq4_nl, q5_0, q5_1; default: f16)' and likewise -ctv for V; '--rpc SERVERS: comma-separated list of RPC servers (host:port)'; '-ngl … (default: auto)'; '--host HOST … (default: 127.0.0.1)'; '-np, --parallel N: number of server slots (default: -1, -1 = auto)'; '--kv-unified … (default: enabled if number of slots is auto)'; -fa auto; --tensor-split; -dev/--device. The quick-start still shows './llama-server -m models/7B/ggml-model.gguf -c 2048'.

llama.cpp src/llama-hparams.cpp (master 2026-08-22): 'uint32_t llama_hparams::n_embd_k_gqa(uint32_t il) const { const uint32_t n_head_kv = this->n_head_kv(il); return n_embd_head_k(il) * n_head_kv; }' and the same for n_embd_v_gqa with n_embd_head_v; per-layer is_swa(il) and is_recr(il) flags select sliding-window and recurrent (n_embd_r/n_embd_s state) handling. Hence f16 KV bytes per token = Σ over attention layers of (n_embd_k_gqa + n_embd_v_gqa) × 2 B — the formula used for every KV figure in this dossier.

llama.cpp ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt default CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES: '50-virtual 61-virtual 70-virtual' only when CUDA < 13 (comment: 50 = 'Maxwell, lowest CUDA 12 standard'); '75-virtual 80-virtual 86-real' always; '89-real 90-virtual' for CUDA ≥ 11.8; '120a-real' for ≥ 12.8; '121a-real' for ≥ 12.9. Consequence: the GTX 970 (compute capability 5.2) hub must be built with its CUDA 12.2 toolchain; a CUDA 13.1 build (RTX 3050 node) drops Maxwell/Pascal/Volta targets.

recommendations: Phase-1 demo model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B at Q8_0, file ggml-org/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF/Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf (28,595,763,552 B = 28.60 GB = 26.6 GiB). With -c 8192 the footprint is ≈29.3 GB (≈27.3 GiB): above the ~25 GB single-node ceiling, ~11 GB beyond the pool's 18 GB VRAM, far below the ≈81 GB pool. Apache-2.0, ungated, AA Intelligence Index v4.1.1 = 52 (#1/137 in its class, 2026-08-22). Record the AA snapshot date and Arena snapshot date in the ADR as the named ranking basis.

Do NOT use a 'marginal' quant (UD-Q6_K_XL 25.3 GB, Gemma 4 Q6_K 25.2 GB, Mistral Small Q8_0 25.05 GB, Qwen3-30B-A3B Q6_K 25.1 GB) to prove the thesis — measure real free RAM per node first (spike) and keep ≥3 GB of margin above the single-node ceiling; Q8_0 of a 27–31B model gives that margin.

Same-class backups, in order: Muse-Glimmer-30B Q8_0 (unsloth, 29.61 GB, Apache-2.0, AA 35) and Gemma 4 31B-it Q8_0 (ggml-org, 32.64 GB, Apache-2.0, AA 30). Both are plain-attention + sliding-window (no recurrent layers), so they are the first thing to try if Qwen3.8's hybrid Gated-DeltaNet layers misbehave over RPC.

Classic plain-transformer fallback if all 2026 hybrids fail over RPC: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B (MIT on HF, ungated; inherits Llama 3.3 licence) or Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (gated) at IQ3_XXS 27.5 GB / Q3_K_M 34.3 GB / IQ4_XS 37.9 GB; budget 320 KiB/token KV (2.7 GB at 8k). Prefer the DeepSeek distill to avoid HF gating friction for friends.

Two-GPU smoke test before the three-node run: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M (ggml-org 18.97 GB) — exceeds the laptop's 8 GB VRAM, fits laptop 8 GB + hub 4 GB + node 6 GB = 18 GB of VRAM with ~0.5 GB KV at 8k, so it proves the RPC split without touching CPU RAM.

Always pass -c explicitly (4096 or 8192). The server default -c 0 loads the model's max context: 262,144 for Qwen3.8-27B (16 GiB KV) and 131,072 for Llama 3.3 70B (40 GiB KV). Keep -ctk/-ctv at the f16 default for Phase 1; revisit q8_0 KV only if measurements require it.

Avoid for v1: gpt-oss-120b (63.4 GB MXFP4 leaves ~17 GB headroom across three OSes and pushes ~45 GB into CPU RAM); Gemma 3 27B and Llama 3.3 70B (HF gate = 'manual' approval per friend, plus Notice/attribution obligations); Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (AA 24, OpenMDW licence adds a new licence to explain for little gain).

research.dossier:
# R05 — Agent platform matrix (Linux deep; macOS/Windows docs-only; packaging outline)

Date verified: 2026-08-22. Primary sources only: systemd man XML at tag v261.2 (GitHub raw; freedesktop.org was unreachable from the research host, and the founder laptop runs systemd 261.2 so the tag matches the fleet), UPower 1.90.9/1.91.2 docs, kernel ABI/cgroup-v2 docs, KDE/GNOME sources at pinned tags, NVIDIA doc PDFs (MPS r590, MIG r580, nvidia-smi), llama.cpp b10581, Apple open-source man pages at pinned tags + Apple developer-doc JSON, Microsoft Learn, Azure Retail Prices API, uv 0.12.5 / pipx 1.16.7 / PyInstaller 6.22.2 / Briefcase 0.4.4 docs. Several items were additionally exercised read-only on the founder laptop (Arch, systemd 261.2, KDE Plasma on Wayland, RTX 2070 Super) and are flagged "(local test)".

## 1. Linux (full depth)

### 1.1 Running the agent: systemd --user + linger
- The agent should be a **user service** (`~/.config/systemd/user/corvid-agent.service`, `WantedBy=default.target`), not a system service: user units are loaded from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user` (~/.config/systemd/user), `/etc/systemd/user`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/systemd/user`, `/usr/lib/systemd/user` (R05-F2); `default.target` is "the main target of the user service manager ... a real unit, not an alias" (R05-F3).
- `loginctl enable-linger USER`: "a user manager is spawned for the user at boot and kept around after logouts. This allows users who are not logged in to run long-running services" (R05-F1). Linger is what makes the hub (solarplexus) and any always-on node keep serving after logout. Founder laptop already has Linger=yes (local test).
- Why user-level rather than root: the owner's own manager is "the final authority" (CLAUDE.md §5.3) and `systemctl --user stop corvid-agent` / `systemctl --user kill` is a kill switch that needs no sudo.

### 1.2 Idle detection — the honest picture (Wayland vs X11, GNOME vs KDE)
There is no single Linux idle API. What actually works, per desktop:
- **logind IdleHint** (`loginctl show-session <id> -p IdleHint`, D-Bus `org.freedesktop.login1` Manager/Session `IdleHint`, `IdleSinceHint`): logind only *reflects* what sessions report; `Session.SetIdleHint()` "is called by the session object to update the idle state of the session whenever it changes", and logind.conf warns IdleAction "requires that user sessions correctly report the idle status" (R05-F13). **GNOME does report it** — gnome-session 50.1 calls `SetIdleHint` (R05-F14). **KDE Plasma apparently does not**: a GitHub code search across org:KDE finds no caller, only copies of the interface XML (R05-F15, unverified/negative evidence). ⇒ IdleHint is trustworthy on GNOME, not on Plasma.
- **KDE `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime`** (the seed's suggestion): kscreenlocker v6.7.4 explicitly returns `NotSupported` ("GetSessionIdleTime is not supported on this platform") when the platform is Wayland; it works only on X11 (R05-F16; reproduced on the founder's Plasma-Wayland laptop). `GetActive` (screen locked?) still works on both.
- **GNOME Wayland**: `org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor` at `/org/gnome/Mutter/IdleMonitor/Core` — `GetIdletime()` (ms) and `AddIdleWatch(interval)` → `WatchFired` signal (mutter 50.4, R05-F17). Plain D-Bus, trivial from Python.
- **Compositor-neutral Wayland**: `ext-idle-notify-v1` (wayland-protocols 1.45, MIT): `ext_idle_notifier_v1.get_idle_notification(timeout_ms, seat)` → `idled`/`resumed`; v2 `get_input_idle_notification` ignores idle inhibitors (R05-F18). KWin v6.7.4 implements it; KIdleTime's Wayland plugin consumes it (R05-F19). Mutter: no implementation found (unverified). Needs a real Wayland client (pywayland or a tiny C/Qt helper), not D-Bus.
- **X11**: XScreenSaverQueryInfo `idle` = "milliseconds since the last input was received from the user on any of the input devices"; `xprintidle` (0.3.0, GPL-2.0-only) prints exactly that (R05-F20).
- **Design consequence**: implement idle as a *presence provider chain* with an explicit "unknown" state: Mutter IdleMonitor → ext-idle-notify (KDE/wlroots) → logind IdleHint → XScreenSaver/xprintidle → unknown. When unknown, the agent must fall back to a *load-based* politeness signal (CPU/IO pressure) and say so in the UI; never silently treat unknown as idle.

### 1.3 Battery / AC
- **UPower** (system bus `org.freedesktop.UPower` at `/org/freedesktop/UPower`): `OnBattery` (b) "Indicates whether the system is running on battery power", `LidIsClosed`; per-device `State` (1 Charging, 2 Discharging, 4 Fully charged), `Percentage` (R05-F21). Founder laptop: upower 1.91.3, on-battery=no (local test).
- **sysfs fallback** (no daemon needed): `/sys/class/power_supply/<name>/type` (Mains/Battery), `online` (AC present), `status` ∈ {Unknown, Charging, Discharging, Not charging, Full}, `capacity` 0–100 (R05-F22). Founder laptop: ADP1 type=Mains online=1; BAT1 status=Not charging capacity=94 (local test).
- Cross-platform shortcut: `psutil.sensors_battery()` → (percent, secsleft, power_plugged) (R05-F53) — same call on all three OSes.

### 1.4 Resource caps — cgroup v2 via systemd, with live changes
- `systemd-run --user [--scope] -p CPUQuota=20% -p MemoryMax=2G ... -- cmd` starts a transient unit; `-p` takes "the same format as systemctl's set-property" (R05-F8). `CPUQuota=20%` "ensures that the executed processes will never get more than 20% CPU time on one CPU" (cpu.max); `MemoryHigh=` is "the main control mechanism", `MemoryMax=` "the last line of defense" (OOM-kills inside the unit); `IOWeight=` 1–10000, default 100 (R05-F4–F6). `CPUWeight=idle` exists for "idle scheduling" (R05-F4 note) and systemd.exec offers `Nice=`, `CPUSchedulingPolicy=idle`, `IOSchedulingClass=idle`, `OOMScoreAdjust=` (R05-F27).
- **Live changes**: `systemctl [--user] set-property UNIT CPUQuota=10% MemoryMax=1G` — "The changes are applied immediately, and stored on disk for future boots, unless --runtime is passed" (R05-F7). This is the mechanism for the owner's slider / "pause while I'm gaming" without restarting jobs. Wrap all CORVID work in one slice (e.g. `corvid.slice` under the user manager) so one set-property call re-caps everything.
- **Delegation gotcha (verified)**: systemd's shipped `user@.service` has `Delegate=pids memory cpu` (R05-F9) — **io is not delegated to user managers**. Local test: `systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=20% -p MemoryMax=100M -p IOWeight=10` produced `cpu.max=20000 100000`, `memory.max=104857600`, but no `io.weight` file (controllers = cpu memory pids) (R05-F10). So CPU/RAM caps work unprivileged out of the box; **disk-I/O caps need a one-time root drop-in** `Delegate=pids memory cpu io` on `user@.service` (R05-F11), or must be done with `IOSchedulingClass=idle` (per-process, no delegation needed).
- Kernel semantics underneath: `cpu.max "$MAX $PERIOD"`, `memory.max` hard limit invoking the OOM killer, `io.weight` [1,10000] default 100 (R05-F12).
- **Kill switch**: `KillMode=control-group` (default) kills "all remaining processes in the control group of this unit" on stop, SIGTERM then SIGKILL after `TimeoutStopSec=`; `systemctl kill --signal=` for instant signalling (R05-F23). Because every job is a transient unit in a CORVID slice, `systemctl --user stop corvid.slice` (or `kill`) is the one-command, no-grace-period kill.

### 1.5 GPU caps — what is real on consumer NVIDIA
- cgroup v2 has **no GPU-compute controller**. Controllers: cpu, memory, io, pids, cpuset, device (BPF), rdma, dmem, hugetlb, misc; the only GPU-adjacent one, `dmem`, "regulates the distribution and accounting of device memory regions" for in-tree DRM drivers (doc example is xe) (R05-F12/F24). Whether the proprietary NVIDIA driver participates is unverified — assume not.
- `nvidia-smi` caps need root: `-pl/--power-limit` ("Requires root", Kepler+, within min/max), `-lgc` lock clocks ("Volta+. Requires root"), `-c/--compute-mode` ("Requires root", resets at reboot) (R05-F25). These are *owner-side* knobs (energy/noise), not per-job shares.
- **MPS** (r590) is aimed at "Hyper-Q capabilities on the latest NVIDIA (Kepler-based) Tesla and Quadro GPUs", Linux-only; Volta+ MPS adds `CUDA_MPS_ACTIVE_THREAD_PERCENTAGE` and `CUDA_MPS_PINNED_DEVICE_MEM_LIMIT` (R05-F26). GeForce support is not stated → open question; do not plan on it.
- **MIG** (r580): Ampere+ with a supported-products table of data-center/RTX PRO parts only — none of the GTX 970 / RTX 2070 Super / RTX 3050 (R05-F27b).
- Therefore GPU "caps" in CORVID are **application-level**: (a) device visibility — `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` or `ggml-rpc-server --device` (R05-F28), or deny `/dev/nvidia*` to a job with systemd `DeviceAllow=`/`DevicePolicy=closed` (R05-F29); (b) VRAM — llama.cpp splits "in proportion to each device's available memory" and `--tensor-split` overrides it; **b10581's rpc-server has no memory-cap flag** (only -t/-d/-H/-p/-c) (R05-F28), so a VRAM ceiling must come from the coordinator's split plan/tensor-split, not the worker; (c) time — the owner's schedule/idle gate simply stops the worker.

## 2. macOS (docs-only)
- **launchd LaunchAgents**: per-user launchd loads `/System/Library/LaunchAgents`, `/Library/LaunchAgents`, and the user's `Library/LaunchAgents`; it "launches any user agents that requested to be running all the time" and sends SIGTERM on logout (R05-F30). Keys (launchd.plist(5), Apple OSS launchd-842.92.1): `KeepAlive`, `RunAtLoad`, `Nice`, `LowPriorityIO`, and `ProcessType` — `Background` jobs get limits "intended to prevent them from disrupting the user experience"; unset ⇒ "light resource limits ... throttling its CPU usage and I/O bandwidth" (R05-F31). That is the free macOS politeness knob; the agent plist should set `ProcessType=Background` (and jobs it spawns inherit via `taskpolicy`).
- Modern registration: `SMAppService` (macOS 13+) registers LaunchAgents/daemons/login items from inside an app bundle (R05-F32) — only relevant if we ever ship a .app; a plain plist in `~/Library/LaunchAgents` is enough for a CLI agent.
- **Idle**: `HIDIdleTime` is the IOHIDSystem registry property `kIOHIDIdleTimeKey = "HIDIdleTime"` published by IOHIDSystem.cpp (IOHIDFamily-2238.120.5) (R05-F33); reading it via `ioreg -c IOHIDSystem` is the conventional path (command form unverified from Apple docs).
- **Battery/AC**: `pmset -g batt` "displays status of batteries and UPSs" (pmset(1), PowerManagement-1846.120.8.0.1); programmatic: IOPowerSources ("uniform access to the state of power sources ... batteries and UPS devices", with change notifications) (R05-F34); or psutil.
- **Caps**: `taskpolicy(8)` (system_cmds-1042.120.1): `-c background|utility|maintenance` QoS clamp, `-b` PRIO_DARWIN_BG, `-d/-g throttle` disk-I/O policy, `-m <MiB>` memory limit, `-p pid` to retarget a running process, `-B` to lift (R05-F35). No cgroup-like hard CPU% on macOS; QoS/background class is the politeness lever.
- **Distribution cost**: notarization is mandatory for Developer-ID software on 10.15+; requires Developer ID cert, Hardened Runtime, secure timestamp, `notarytool` (altool/Xcode≤13 rejected since 2023-11-01) (R05-F36/F37). Apple Developer Program "Enrollment is 99 USD ... per membership year" (R05-F38). Unsigned/unnotarized binaries hit Gatekeeper warnings (R05-F39) — exactly the "unsigned-app warnings scare members" risk in CLAUDE.md §11.

## 3. Windows (docs-only)
- **Idle**: `GetLastInputInfo` "is useful for input idle detection. However, GetLastInputInfo does not provide system-wide user input information across all running sessions ... only the session that invoked the function"; `LASTINPUTINFO.dwTime` is a tick count, "not guaranteed to be incremental" (R05-F40). **Services "cannot directly interact with a user as of Windows Vista"** (Session 0) (R05-F41) ⇒ a Windows service cannot see the user's idle time. Conclusion: run the Windows agent **in the user session** — `schtasks /create /sc ONLOGON ... /it` ("run the scheduled task only when the run as user ... is logged on") or a tray app — not as a service (R05-F42). Task Scheduler's own idle model (Win8+: user absent after 4 min without keyboard/mouse; resource checks every 10 min / 30 s; re-checks on AC/DC and battery events) and `ITaskSettings.StopIfGoingOnBatteries` / `DisallowStartIfOnBatteries` are available for free (R05-F43/F44).
- **Battery/AC**: `GetSystemPowerStatus` → `SYSTEM_POWER_STATUS.ACLineStatus` 0 Offline / 1 Online / 255 Unknown, `BatteryLifePercent`, `SystemStatusFlag` (battery saver) (R05-F45); push notifications via `RegisterPowerSettingNotification` with `GUID_ACDC_POWER_SOURCE` (PoAc/PoDc/PoHot), `GUID_BATTERY_PERCENTAGE_REMAINING`, `GUID_POWER_SAVING_STATUS`, and user-presence GUIDs (`GUID_SESSION_USER_PRESENCE` for user-mode apps; `GUID_GLOBAL_USER_PRESENCE` only for session-0 services, Win8+) (R05-F46).
- **Caps = Job Objects**: CPU hard cap via `JOBOBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_INFORMATION` (`CpuRate` = percent×100 of 10,000, `JOB_OBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_HARD_CAP`; Win8+); committed-memory caps via `JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION.ProcessMemoryLimit/JobMemoryLimit`; `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_AFFINITY`, `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PRIORITY_CLASS`; `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`; IO caps (`MaxIops/MaxBandwidth`, Win10+); **kill switch** = `TerminateJobObject` ("Terminates all processes currently associated with the job" incl. nested jobs) (R05-F47–F49). Plus `SetPriorityClass(IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS | PROCESS_MODE_BACKGROUND_BEGIN)` as the cheap politeness lever (R05-F50).
- **Code signing cost**: Azure Trusted Signing retail price (Azure Retail Prices API, Global): Basic 9.99 USD/month (5,000 signatures/month), Premium 99.99 USD/month, overage 0.005 USD/signature; Public-Trust identities for organizations in listed countries, **individual developers only in US/Canada** (R05-F51/F52). Unsigned or no-reputation binaries: SmartScreen "presents a warning to the user" (R05-F53b). Traditional OV/IV certificates from CAs exist (SSL.com lists IV "no business docs required") but prices were not extractable (unverified).

## 4. Opt-in model — design notes
- Borrow BOINC's vocabulary verbatim (lib/prefs.h): `run_on_batteries`, `run_if_user_active`, `run_gpu_if_user_active`, `suspend_if_no_recent_input` (minutes), `idle_time_to_run`, `cpu_usage_limit` (%), `max_ncpus_pct`, `ram_max_used_busy_frac` / `ram_max_used_idle_frac`, `suspend_cpu_usage`, `start_hour`/`end_hour` (R05-F54). These map 1:1 onto: idle gate (§1.2), battery gate (§1.3), CPUQuota/AllowedCPUs, MemoryHigh/Max, "suspend when host CPU busy", and schedule.
- Every role is a separate opt-in bit: `inference_host`, `batch_jobs`, `gpu_allowed`, `disk_donate_gb`, plus schedule + caps. Default: all off. The agent enforces locally; the coordinator only reads.
- "Unknown presence" (§1.2) must be a first-class state shown in the tray/status page.

## 5. Packaging (outline)
- **Python + uv** (0.12.5): one installer line per OS (`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`, PowerShell `irm ... | iex`), `uv python install` fetches Astral python-build-standalone ("Python does not publish official distributable binaries"), `uv tool install corvid-agent` gives an isolated venv with the executable on PATH; `uv self update`; MIT/Apache-2.0 (R05-F55/F56). **pipx** (1.16.7, MIT) is the same idea without Python management (R05-F57). Neither needs code signing; friends see a terminal for 30 s and no unsigned-app dialog for the agent itself (uv's own installer is signed by Astral — out of our hands).
- **PyInstaller** (6.22.2): one-file mode unpacks to a temp `_MEIxxxxxx` folder on every start ("a little slower to start"); `--windowed` makes a .app; `--codesign-identity` enables hardened runtime and "requires ... a valid Apple-issued code signing certificate"; GPL-2.0-with-exception (bundled apps may be closed/any licence) (R05-F58/F59). **Briefcase** (0.4.4, BSD-3) produces .app / MSI / Linux packages and documents the signing-identity chores (R05-F60). Both single-binary routes reintroduce notarization ($99/yr) and Windows signing ($9.99/mo) — the exact "$0 budget" and "installer support burden" costs CLAUDE.md §11 warns about.
- Recommendation below: v1 = uv-based install script + systemd/launchd/Task-Scheduler registration; revisit single binary only in Phase 4 if non-technical onboarding demands it.

## 6. Local verification summary (founder laptop, 2026-08-22)
systemd 261.2, cgroup2fs; KDE Plasma, XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland; Linger=yes; user manager controllers `cpu memory pids` (DelegateControllers); transient scope honoured CPUQuota/MemoryMax, ignored IOWeight; `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime` → "not supported on this platform"; `org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor` absent (expected); upower 1.91.3 on-battery=no; sysfs ADP1 online=1 / BAT1 capacity=94.

facts.statement: loginctl enable-linger USER: "If enabled for a specific user, a user manager is spawned for the user at boot and kept around after logouts. This allows users who are not logged in to run long-running services."

User-mode unit load path (systemd --user) includes $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user (~/.config/systemd/user, 'User configuration'), $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS/systemd/user, /etc/systemd/user, $XDG_DATA_HOME/systemd/user, /usr/local/lib/systemd/user and /usr/lib/systemd/user.

For the user service manager, default.target "is the main target of the user service manager, started by default when the service manager is invoked ... it is a real unit, not an alias" (so user services use WantedBy=default.target).

CPUQuota= controls cpu.max on cgroup v2; "Takes a percentage value ... relative to the total CPU time available on one CPU. Use values > 100% for allotting CPU time on more than one CPU." Example in the man page: "CPUQuota=20% ensures that the executed processes will never get more than 20% CPU time on one CPU." CPUWeight= accepts the special value "idle" (cpu.idle) so the cgroup gets CPU only when nothing else wants it.

MemoryMax= is the "absolute limit on memory usage ... If memory usage cannot be contained under the limit, out-of-memory killer is invoked inside the unit. It is recommended to use MemoryHigh= as the main control mechanism and use MemoryMax= as the last line of defense." MemoryHigh= is a throttling limit ("processes are heavily slowed down and memory is taken away aggressively"). Both accept K/M/G/T suffixes or a percentage of installed RAM.

IOWeight= "Takes a single weight value (between 1 and 10000) to set the default block I/O weight. This controls the io.weight control group attribute, which defaults to 100 ... The available I/O bandwidth is split up among all units within one slice relative to their block I/O weight."

systemctl set-property UNIT PROPERTY=VALUE: "Set the specified unit properties at runtime where this is supported ... many resource control settings (primarily those in systemd.resource-control(5)) may. The changes are applied immediately, and stored on disk for future boots, unless --runtime is passed, in which case the settings only apply until the next reboot." Example: systemctl set-property foobar.service CPUWeight=200 MemoryMax=2G IPAccounting=yes; empty assignment resets to default.

systemd-run: --property=/-p "Sets a property on the scope or service unit that is created. This option takes an assignment in the same format as systemctl(1)'s set-property command"; --scope creates a transient .scope (executed by systemd-run itself, synchronous); --user targets the per-user manager (root slice by default, --slice= to choose); man page example: "systemd-run -p IOWeight=10 updatedb" and "systemd-run --scope --user screen".

The shipped user@.service unit template sets "Delegate=pids memory cpu" (plus DelegateSubgroup=init.scope, KillMode=mixed, Slice=user-%i.slice): only the pids, memory and cpu controllers are delegated to per-user service managers by default — io is not.
facts.version: systemd v261.2; identical line present in /usr/lib/systemd/system/user@.service on the founder laptop (systemd 261.2-1-arch)

facts.statement: (local test, founder laptop, systemd 261.2, cgroup2fs, KDE/Wayland) `systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=20% -p MemoryMax=100M -p IOWeight=10 -- sh -c ...` created app.slice/<unit>.scope with cpu.max="20000 100000" and memory.max=104857600 applied, but no io.weight file existed (cgroup.controllers = "cpu memory pids"; `systemctl show user@1000.service -p DelegateControllers` = "cpu memory pids"). CPU/RAM caps work unprivileged; IOWeight is silently ineffective for --user units unless io is delegated.
facts.version: systemd 261.2 on Arch (founder laptop); kernel cgroup v2

facts.statement: Delegate= "Takes either a boolean argument or a (possibly empty) list of control group controller names. If true, delegation is turned on, and all supported controllers are enabled for the unit"; delegation makes the unit's cgroup subtree the exclusive property of the delegatee (systemd won't touch sub-cgroups). Hence a root-owned drop-in on user@.service (e.g. Delegate=pids memory cpu io) is the documented way to let per-user managers apply io.weight/io.max.
facts.version: systemd v261.2 (see also docs/CGROUP_DELEGATION.md at v261.2)

facts.statement: Kernel cgroup v2: cpu.max is "$MAX $PERIOD" (default "max 100000"); memory.max is the "Memory usage hard limit ... If a cgroup's memory usage reaches this limit and can't be reduced, the OOM killer is invoked in the cgroup"; io.weight range [1,10000], default 100. Controllers documented: cpu, memory, io, pid, cpuset, device (BPF-based, no interface files), rdma, dmem ("regulates the distribution and accounting of device memory regions"; example shows DRM xe vram), hugetlb, misc. There is no GPU-compute controller.

org.freedesktop.login1: Manager.IdleHint "reflects the idle hint state of the system"; IdleSinceHint/IdleSinceHintMonotonic are timestamps of the last change; Session.SetIdleHint(b) "is called by the session object to update the idle state of the session whenever it changes". logind.conf IdleAction= "requires that user sessions correctly report the idle status to the system" — logind does not measure graphical idleness itself.
facts.version: systemd v261.2 (IdleAction text from man/logind.conf.xml at the same tag)

facts.statement: GNOME reports idleness to logind: gnome-session 50.1 gsm-systemd.c calls org.freedesktop.login1.Session "SetIdleHint" with the session's idle boolean ("Updating systemd idle status"). So loginctl IdleHint is meaningful on GNOME sessions.

No KDE Plasma component appears to call logind SetIdleHint: a GitHub code search for SetIdleHint in org:KDE returned only interface-XML copies (plasma-login-manager, systemdgenie), no caller in kwin/powerdevil/kscreenlocker. Treat loginctl IdleHint as unreliable on Plasma until proven otherwise on a real idle Plasma session.
facts.version: KDE org default branches as indexed by GitHub code search on 2026-08-22 (negative evidence)

facts.statement: KDE kscreenlocker's org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime() returns a D-Bus NotSupported error ("GetSessionIdleTime is not supported on this platform") when KWindowSystem::isPlatformWayland(); on X11 it returns KIdleTime::instance()->idleTime(). Reproduced on the founder's Plasma-Wayland laptop via busctl (Call failed: GetSessionIdleTime is not supported on this platform). GetActive/GetActiveTime (lock state) remain available.

GNOME/Mutter exposes org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor ("used by gnome-desktop to implement user activity monitoring") with GetIdletime() -> t (idle time), AddIdleWatch(interval ms) -> id firing WatchFired, AddUserActiveWatch, RemoveWatch; object path /org/gnome/Mutter/IdleMonitor/Core. gnome-shell 50.4 also exposes org.gnome.ScreenSaver GetActive/GetActiveTime/ActiveChanged (lock state).

Wayland ext-idle-notify-v1 (staging, wayland-protocols 1.45, MIT, (c) Martin Gräßlin 2015 / Simon Ser 2022): ext_idle_notifier_v1.get_idle_notification(timeout ms, wl_seat) creates an ext_idle_notification_v1 that emits idled after no user activity for the timeout and resumed when activity returns; version 2 adds get_input_idle_notification which "ignores idle inhibitors" and counts only keyboard/mouse input.

KWin implements ext-idle-notify-v1 (src/wayland/idlenotify_v1.cpp implements ext_idle_notifier_v1 incl. get_input_idle_notification) and KIdleTime's Wayland plugin consumes ext_idle_notifier_v1/ext_idle_notification_v1 — so on Plasma Wayland this protocol is the supported idle source. No ext-idle-notify implementation was found in GNOME/mutter (GitHub code search) — unverified negative.

X11: the MIT-SCREEN-SAVER extension's XScreenSaverQueryInfo returns an idle field that "specifies the number of milliseconds since the last input was received from the user on any of the input devices"; xprintidle 0.3.0 is a GPL-2.0-only utility that "queries the X server for the user's idle time and prints it to stdout (in milliseconds)" using Xss (libXss).

This property is provided for convenience."), LidIsClosed, LidIsPresent, DaemonVersion; Device properties include Type, Percentage, State (0 Unknown, 1 Charging, 2 Discharging, 3 Empty, 4 Fully charged, 5 Pending charge, 6 Pending discharge), TimeToEmpty/TimeToFull. facts.statement: sysfs power_supply ABI: /sys/class/power_supply/<name>/status valid values "Unknown", "Charging", "Discharging", "Not charging", "Full"; /capacity = 0-100 percent; /online indicates the supply (e.g. AC adapter) is present/online. systemd.kill: KillMode= defaults to control-group — "all remaining processes in the control group of this unit will be killed on unit stop"; processes get KillSignal= (default SIGTERM, followed by SIGCONT), then SIGKILL/FinalKillSignal= after TimeoutStopSec= (unless SendSIGKILL=no). systemctl kill PATTERN sends an arbitrary signal (--signal=, --kill-whom=) to a unit's processes.
facts.version: systemd v261.2 (systemctl kill from man/systemctl.xml at same tag)

Windows services: "Services cannot directly interact with a user as of Windows Vista" (Session 0 isolation); suggested workarounds are WTSSendMessage or CreateProcessAsUser into the user's session. Services "can execute even when no user is logged on"; sc.exe create supports start= boot|system|auto|demand|disabled|delayed-auto and obj= account.

schtasks /create: /sc ONLOGON "runs whenever a user (any user) logs on"; /sc ONIDLE with /i <idletime> runs when the system is idle; /it "Specifies to run the scheduled task only when the run as user ... is logged on to the computer" (interactive-only); /ru and /rl set run-as user and run level.

Task Scheduler idle conditions: in Windows 8+ "Task Scheduler relies on the operating system power subsystem to detect user presence. By default, the user is considered absent after four minutes of no keyboard or mouse input"; resource checks every 10 minutes when present, 30 seconds when away, plus re-checks on 'User presence state changed', 'AC/DC power source changed', 'Battery level changed'; Windows 7 used 15-minute checks with >90% idle CPU/disk.

GetSystemPowerStatus "indicates whether the system is running on AC or DC power, whether the battery is currently charging, how much battery life remains, and if battery saver is on or off"; SYSTEM_POWER_STATUS.ACLineStatus: 0 Offline, 1 Online, 255 Unknown; BatteryFlag bits (1 high >66%, 2 low <33%, 4 critical...), BatteryLifePercent 0-100/255, SystemStatusFlag (battery saver).

recommendations: Linux agent = a per-user systemd service (~/.config/systemd/user/corvid-agent.service, WantedBy=default.target) plus `loginctl enable-linger` on always-on nodes (hub, optiplex); never a root service. Kill switch = `systemctl --user stop corvid.slice` (all CORVID work lives in one user slice) — KillMode=control-group guarantees nothing survives.

Run every job as a transient unit: `systemd-run --user --slice=corvid.slice -p CPUQuota=<n>% -p MemoryHigh=<x> -p MemoryMax=<y> -p CPUWeight=idle -p IOSchedulingClass=idle -p Nice=19 ...`; implement the owner's live slider as `systemctl --user set-property corvid.slice CPUQuota=... MemoryMax=...` (applied immediately, persisted unless --runtime).

Document the io-delegation gotcha in the Linux install guide: CPU/RAM caps work unprivileged; IOWeight/IOReadBandwidthMax need a one-time sudo drop-in `/etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/corvid.conf` with `[Service]\nDelegate=pids memory cpu io` (spike this on the hub; until then rely on IOSchedulingClass=idle).

Build idle detection as a provider chain with an explicit UNKNOWN state: (1) org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor.GetIdletime (GNOME, D-Bus), (2) ext-idle-notify-v1 client (KDE/wlroots Wayland — small helper; spike pywayland vs a 50-line C/Qt binary), (3) logind IdleHint (trust only when provider 1 is present/GNOME), (4) XScreenSaver/xprintidle (X11), (5) UNKNOWN → use load/pressure heuristics and show 'presence unknown' in the status page. Do not use org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime (NotSupported on Plasma Wayland).

Battery/AC: use psutil.sensors_battery() as the one cross-platform call; on Linux fall back to /sys/class/power_supply/*/online + status when psutil is unavailable; default policy run_on_batteries=false, and on AC-loss pause immediately (don't wait for the next heartbeat).

GPU policy for the spec: treat GPU as all-or-nothing per job/time-window — no compute shares on GeForce (no MIG; MPS is Tesla/Quadro-targeted and Linux-only; cgroup v2 has no GPU controller). Implement 'GPU off' via DeviceAllow/DevicePolicy=closed or CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' on the job unit, and VRAM ceilings via the coordinator's --tensor-split plan (ggml-rpc-server b10581 has no --mem flag). Owner-side nvidia-smi -pl power caps are root-only — document as optional sudo step, never required.

macOS agent = LaunchAgent plist in ~/Library/LaunchAgents with KeepAlive=true, RunAtLoad=true, ProcessType=Background, LowPriorityIO=true, Nice=10+; spawn jobs via `taskpolicy -c background` (and -m MiB for a memory limit); idle via IOHIDSystem HIDIdleTime (ioreg) + org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver-equivalent lock check; battery via pmset -g batt/psutil. Defer SMAppService/.app bundle until a tray UI exists.

Windows agent = per-user Scheduled Task (ONLOGON, /it, highest-available run level not required) running the Python agent in the user session — NOT a Windows service — because GetLastInputInfo is session-scoped and services live in Session 0. Use Job Objects for each job (CPU hard cap via CpuRate, JobMemoryLimit, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, TerminateJobObject as kill switch) and register GUID_ACDC_POWER_SOURCE / GUID_SESSION_USER_PRESENCE notifications; also set Task Scheduler StopIfGoingOnBatteries for belt-and-braces.

Packaging v1 (Phases 2–3): Python 3.12+ app published as a wheel, installed with `uv tool install corvid-agent` (uv manages Python via python-build-standalone); one install script per OS that also registers the systemd/launchd/Task-Scheduler unit; `uv tool upgrade` for updates. This keeps the $0 budget (no Apple $99/yr, no Trusted Signing $9.99/mo) and avoids Gatekeeper/SmartScreen dialogs for our own code. Revisit PyInstaller/Briefcase single binaries in Phase 4 only if non-technical onboarding fails; budget $99/yr (Apple) + $9.99/mo (Azure Trusted Signing, individual identity requires US/Canada) if that day comes, and note PyInstaller needs per-OS build machines.

Opt-in schema (coordinator DB + agent config): boolean roles {inference_host, batch_jobs, gpu_allowed, disk_donate}, caps {cpu_quota_pct, allowed_cpus, mem_high, mem_max, io_weight|io_idle, vram_cap_mb (coordinator-enforced)}, politeness {run_if_user_active=false, idle_minutes, run_on_batteries=false, suspend_cpu_usage_pct, schedule windows} — borrow BOINC's names so the semantics are already documented; the agent enforces locally and reports the effective policy in its heartbeat.
Add ADR: 'Idle/presence detection is best-effort and desktop-specific; UNKNOWN presence never counts as idle' and 'GPU sharing is temporal, not spatial, on consumer NVIDIA'.
open_questions: Does KDE Plasma (powerdevil/kwin 6.x) ever call logind SetIdleHint? Negative code-search evidence only — confirm by leaving a Plasma Wayland session idle past the power-saving timeout and watching `loginctl show-session -p IdleHint`.
Does GNOME Mutter (50.x) implement ext-idle-notify-v1? Code search found nothing; if not, the provider chain must keep the Mutter D-Bus path as a separate branch (it does today).

Which Wayland client route for ext-idle-notify-v1 from a Python agent: pywayland (pure Python, needs scanner-generated bindings) vs a tiny C/Qt helper binary vs depending on a distro-packaged tool (e.g. swayidle)? Spike on the founder's Plasma laptop.

Does CUDA MPS actually start on GeForce (Turing/Ampere) with driver 535/CUDA 12.2 (hub GTX 970, Maxwell) and CUDA 13.1 (RTX 3050)? The doc scopes MPS to Tesla/Quadro; a 10-minute spike (nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d, then a CUDA client) settles whether active-thread-percentage caps are even an option.
Does the NVIDIA proprietary driver integrate with the cgroup v2 dmem controller (kernel 6.14+)? If yes, VRAM caps per job become possible on Linux; if no (expected), VRAM stays coordinator-planned.

Does the older llama.cpp rpc-server still used on the hub (driver 535/CUDA 12.2 may force an older build) have the removed -m/--mem flag? Pin the exact llama.cpp tag per node and check `ggml-rpc-server --help`.

On the hub with Tailscale in userspace mode, is there a tailscale0 interface to bind ggml-rpc-server/agent listeners to at all? (Out of R05 scope but gates the 'bind to tailnet interface only' rule on that node.)
