facts.statement: Grafana's repository LICENSE at tag v13.2.0 is the GNU Affero General Public License v3; LICENSING.md states 'The default license for this project is AGPL-3.0-only' and lists Apache-2.0 sub-directories (packages/grafana-data, grafana-e2e-selectors, grafana-runtime, grafana-ui, packaging/, kinds/, pkg/kinds/, pkg/kindsys/, pkg/registry/schemas/, grafana-mixin/, …) and public/vendor under upstream licences. v13.2.0 was published 2026-08-18.
facts.version: grafana v13.2.0 (LICENSE + LICENSING.md at tag; release date via https://api.github.com/repos/grafana/grafana/releases/latest)

facts.statement: Grafana Labs' licensing page: 'On April 20, 2021, Grafana Labs announced that going forward, our core open source projects will be moving from the Apache License v2.0 to AGPLv3.' Grafana, Loki and Tempo are AGPLv3; those who modify and offer it as a service and do not want AGPL obligations 'can contact us to secure a commercial license'; a non-AGPL, proprietary-licensed Enterprise binary is available free, with paid licence keys unlocking enterprise features.

Grafana docs: 'Grafana Enterprise is a commercial edition of Grafana that includes additional features not found in the open source version.' Enterprise-only features listed: role-based access control, data source permissions, data source query/resource caching, reporting and PDF export, custom branding, usage insights, recorded queries, Vault integration, auditing, request security, settings updates at runtime, team sync, enhanced LDAP, SAML, protected roles, premium data source plugins (40+). None of these is needed for a friends-scale status page.

Grafana Docker docs: images are `grafana/grafana` (Open Source) and `grafana/grafana-enterprise`; 'The recommended and default edition of Grafana is Grafana Enterprise. It is free and includes all the features of the OSS edition.' Caution: 'Starting with Grafana release 12.4.0, the grafana/grafana-oss Docker Hub repository will no longer be updated… use the grafana/grafana Docker Hub repository.' Default port 3000; persistent data at /var/lib/grafana; any config key can be set via env `GF_<SectionName>_<KeyName>`.
facts.version: docs 'latest' as of 2026-08-22 (note applies from Grafana 12.4.0)

facts.statement: Grafana 'ships with the PostgreSQL data source out of the box' (PostgreSQL 9.0 and newer). Configure page warning: 'the database user you specify should have only SELECT permissions on the relevant schemas and tables. Grafana does not validate the safety of queries, so users could run potentially harmful SQL (for example, DROP TABLE). Create a dedicated PostgreSQL user with restricted permissions.' TLS modes: disable / require / verify-ca / verify-full.

Grafana OSS visualizations relevant to a node map, none marked enterprise-only or beta on the index page: State timeline ('for state changes over time'), Status history ('for periodic state over time'), Stat ('for big stats and optional sparkline'), Gauge ('how far a single metric is from a threshold'), Table, Geomap, Node graph ('for directed graphs or networks'), Canvas ('explicitly place elements within static and dynamic layouts').

Grafana thresholds: 'A threshold is a value or limit you set for a metric that's reflected visually when it's met or exceeded'; modes Absolute ('defined by a number') or Percentage ('relative to minimum or maximum'); defaults Base=green, 80=red, Mode=Absolute; supported by Bar chart, Bar gauge, Candlestick, Canvas, Gauge, Geomap, Histogram, Stat, State timeline, Status history, Table, Time series, Trend — i.e. ADR-0001's 'distance to next product threshold' maps directly onto Stat/Gauge/Bar gauge thresholds.

Grafana config defaults that a tailnet-only, no-logging deployment must override: [dashboards] min_refresh_interval default 5 seconds ('prevents users from setting the dashboard refresh interval to a lower value'); [server] http_addr empty 'is equivalent to setting the value to 0.0.0.0, which means the Grafana service binds to all interfaces' (set it to the tailnet IP or 127.0.0.1 per CLAUDE.md §5.6); http_port default 3000; [analytics] reporting_enabled default true ('Grafana sends anonymous usage statistics to stats.grafana.org'); check_for_updates default true; [auth] disable_login_form default false; [security] cookie_secure default false.

Grafana anonymous access: [auth.anonymous] keys enabled, org_name ('Organization name that should be used for unauthenticated users'), org_role (Viewer by default; 'other valid values are Editor and Admin'), hide_version, device_limit ('Limits the number of anonymous devices in your instance'). In Grafana Enterprise 'anonymous access is licensed as active users' (1 user per 3 devices) — irrelevant for the OSS build.

Grafana auth proxy: [auth.proxy] enabled=true, header_name = X-WEBAUTH-USER, header_property = username|email, auto_sign_up = true (creates users on first sight), sync_ttl = 15, whitelist = (list of proxy IPs; 'This can be used to prevent users spoofing the X-WEBAUTH-USER header'), headers = Name:X-WEBAUTH-NAME Email:X-WEBAUTH-EMAIL, enable_login_token = false. This is how a Tailscale identity header (mapped by Caddy header_up) becomes a Grafana login with zero passwords.

Grafana provisioning: data sources and dashboards are provisioned from YAML under the provisioning directory (conf/provisioning, or /etc/grafana/provisioning on deb/rpm); 'each configuration file contains a list of data sources, under the datasources key'; dashboard providers point at a folder of JSON dashboards; updateIntervalSeconds ≤10 makes Grafana watch the filesystem; allowUiUpdates controls whether UI edits persist (provisioned files win on reload). Enables dashboards-as-code in the CORVID repo.
Caddy's LICENSE at tag v2.11.4 is the Apache License, Version 2.0; v2.11.4 was published 2026-06-03.

Caddy reverse_proxy: syntax `reverse_proxy [<matcher>] [<upstreams...>] { … }`; by default passes incoming headers including Host unmodified but sets/augments X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host; 'For these X-Forwarded-* headers, by default, the proxy will ignore their values from incoming requests, to prevent spoofing' (trust via the `servers > trusted_proxies` global option); `header_up [+|-]<field> [<value|regexp> [<replacement>]]` / `header_down` modify proxied headers (`header_up -Some-Header` deletes); upstream forms include localhost:4000, http://localhost:4000, h2c://127.0.0.1, unix//var/php.sock; flush_interval controls streaming.

Caddy handle_path 'Works the same as the handle directive, but implicitly uses uri strip_prefix to strip the matched path prefix'; `handle_path /api/* { reverse_proxy localhost:9000 }` forwards with /api removed. Therefore ADR-0003's `/status` → `:8092` should use `handle_path /status/*` only if the status app is mounted at root, and `handle /status/*` if the app knows its own prefix.

Caddy forward_auth 'proxies a clone of the request to an authentication gateway'; 'If the upstream responds with a 2xx status code, then access is granted', otherwise the upstream's response is returned; `copy_headers` lists 'HTTP header fields to copy from the response to the original request' with `Before>After` renaming; it is sugar over reverse_proxy. Caddy's docs include a Tailscale example: `forward_auth unix//run/tailscale.nginx-auth.sock { uri /auth; header_up Remote-Addr {remote_host}; header_up Remote-Port {remote_port}; header_up Original-URI {uri}; copy_headers { Tailscale-User>X-Webauth-User Tailscale-Name>X-Webauth-Name Tailscale-Login>X-Webauth-Login Tailscale-Tailnet>X-Webauth-Tailnet Tailscale-Profile-Picture>X-Webauth-Profile-Picture } }`.

Caddy bind 'Overrides the interface to which the server's socket should bind'; `bind <hosts...>` (addresses, no port; e.g. `bind 10.0.0.1`, `bind 127.0.0.1 [::1]`); by default 'the listener binds to the empty (wildcard) interface'; 'Virtual hosts are not shared across different listeners'. This is the directive that satisfies CLAUDE.md §5.6 for Caddy (bind the tailnet IP in kernel mode; 127.0.0.1 in userspace mode — see R07-F26).

Caddy log directive 'Enables and configures HTTP request logging (also known as access logs)'; 'By default, headers with potentially sensitive information (Cookie, Set-Cookie, Authorization and Proxy-Authorization) will be logged as REDACTED' (disable via the log_credentials global option). The page documents no option to log request bodies.

Caddy automatic HTTPS for Tailscale: 'Domains ending in .ts.net will not be managed by Caddy. Instead, Caddy will automatically attempt to get these certificates at handshake-time from the locally-running Tailscale instance'; requires 'HTTPS is enabled in your Tailscale account' and Caddy running as root or tailscaled configured to let the caddy user fetch certs. Tailscale KB (validated 2026-01-05): 'Starting with the beta release of Caddy 2.5'; set `TS_PERMIT_CERT_UID=caddy` in /etc/default/tailscaled; a site block named `machine-name.domain-alias.ts.net` 'automatically enables HTTPS'.
facts.version: KB validated 2026-01-05; Caddy docs https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https as of 2026-08-22

facts.statement: Tailscale HTTPS certificates KB (validated 2025-12-10): MagicDNS is a prerequisite; `tailscale cert` requests a Let's Encrypt certificate (90-day expiry, renewal is the user's job unless Caddy integrates); certificate names become part of public Certificate Transparency logs — 'Do not enable the HTTPS feature if any of your machine names contain sensitive information' (names are <machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net); frequent requests can hit Let's Encrypt rate limits ('waiting 34 hours').

Caddy Linux service: the systemd unit reads /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, runs as user/group caddy, config is applied with `sudo systemctl reload caddy`, which talks to the admin API at localhost:2019. The `import` directive 'includes a snippet or file' and accepts globs (`import sites-enabled/*`), works anywhere including inside site blocks — so CORVID can own a drop-in route file instead of editing the hub's existing Caddyfile.

Tailscale Serve KB (validated 2026-01-20): Serve adds `Tailscale-User-Login`, `Tailscale-User-Name`, `Tailscale-User-Profile-Pic` to proxied requests; 'These identity headers are not populated for traffic originating from tagged devices'; headers apply to tailnet traffic, not Funnel; 'Tailscale Serve requires you to enable HTTPS certificates in your tailnet.' The page does not mention a plain-HTTP (`--http`) mode.

tailscale v1.102.3 source, ipn/ipnlocal/serve.go `addTailscaleIdentityHeaders` (lines ~1078-1107): first DELETES any incoming `Tailscale-User-Login`, `Tailscale-User-Name`, `Tailscale-User-Profile-Pic`, `Tailscale-Funnel-Request`, `Tailscale-Headers-Info` ('Clear any incoming values squatting in the headers'); for Funnel sets `Tailscale-Funnel-Request: ?1` and returns; calls `b.WhoIs("tcp", srcAddr)`; returns without headers if the source is not a tailnet peer or `node.IsTagged()` ('Not setting identity headers for tagged nodes'); otherwise sets Login/Name (RFC 2047 Q-encoded if non-ASCII) and Profile-Pic plus `Tailscale-Headers-Info: https://tailscale.com/s/serve-headers`. `addProxyForwardedHeaders` sets X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto (https only when TLS) and X-Forwarded-For = peer's tailnet IP. Both run in the ReverseProxy Rewrite hook for every serve web handler (line ~959-981), not only TLS ones.
facts.version: tailscale v1.102.3 (published 2026-08-20); hub runs 1.98.4 — re-check at upgrade

facts.statement: tailscale v1.102.3 CLI (cmd/tailscale/cli/serve_v2.go ~line 239-251): `tailscale serve` accepts `--bg`, `--set-path`, `--https=<port>` ('default mode'), and — for `serve` only, not `funnel` — `--http=<port>` ('Expose an HTTP server at the specified port'), plus `--tcp`, `--tls-terminated-tcp`, `--yes`. The interactive 'enable HTTPS certificates' flow (`enableFeatureInteractive(... CapabilityHTTPS)`) is invoked only when the serve type is HTTPS (lines ~461-473). Runtime confirmation that identity headers appear on a `--http` listener is S-05's job.

`tailscale whois [--json] [--proto tcp|udp] ip[:port]` 'shows the machine and user associated with a Tailscale IP (v4 or v6)' (cmd/tailscale/cli/whois.go; KB 1080 validated 2026-07-30: 'Get the machine and user associated with a Tailscale IP'). Output: Machine Name/ID/Addresses and, for untagged nodes, User Name (LoginName) and ID; for tagged nodes it prints Tags instead of a User. JSON form is apitype.WhoIsResponse {Node, UserProfile, CapMap}.

LocalAPI whois (ipn/localapi/localapi.go v1.102.3): route `whois` → `GET /localapi/v0/whois?addr=<ip | ip:port | nodekey>[&proto=tcp|udp]` over the tailscaled unix socket; requires a valid Host header ("local-tailscaled.sock" or empty; loopback only with password) and no Referer/Origin; needs PermitRead. ipn/ipnserver/server.go `actor.Permissions`: for a unix-socket connection `read = true` for every local client (write only for root/operator); safesocket: socket mode 0666 on peer-credential platforms (Linux); default path /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock (paths.go). So an unprivileged coordinator process on Linux can call whois without sudo.
facts.version: tailscale v1.102.3; also ipn/ipnserver/server.go, safesocket/safesocket.go + unixsocket.go, paths/paths.go at the same tag

facts.statement: Userspace-networking inbound path (wgengine/netstack/netstack.go v1.102.3, acceptTCP/forwardTCP): for an inbound TCP connection whose destination is this node's own Tailscale IP, `case isTailscaleIP: dialIP = ipv4Loopback` — tailscaled dials `127.0.0.1:<port>` on the host with a standard net.Dialer and copies bytes; if the dial fails it logs 'could not connect to local backend server' and RSTs. After dialing it calls `ns.pm.RegisterIPPortIdentity("tcp", backendLocalIPPort, clientRemoteIP)` so the loopback (IP:ephemeral-port) of that forwarded connection maps to the peer. `LocalBackend.WhoIs` (ipn/ipnlocal/local.go) first looks the IP up as a node; if not found and a port is given it asks `ProxyMapper().WhoIsIPPort(proto, ipp)`. Consequences on a userspace-mode hub: listeners must be on 127.0.0.1 (or wildcard), the app sees 127.0.0.1 as client, and whois must be called with ip:port (client source port), as `tailscale nginx-auth` / Caddy's forward_auth example do via Remote-Addr + Remote-Port. Serve handlers are dispatched from the same netstack path (`ns.lb.TCPHandlerForDst`).
facts.version: tailscale v1.102.3 (netstack.go acceptTCP ~L1530-1738, forwardTCP ~L1743-1800; local.go WhoIs ~L1698-1738). solarplexus runs 1.98.4 in userspace mode (R00-F2)

facts.statement: Tailscale's userspace-networking KB (validated 2025-11-12) documents only the outbound side (`--tun=userspace-networking`; SOCKS5/HTTP proxy via ALL_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY); it says nothing about inbound connections or Serve. Tailscale's Docker parameters page (validated 2026-03-23) says TS_USERSPACE 'Controls whether to use userspace networking instead of kernel networking. Enabled by default' and TS_SERVE_CONFIG 'Accepts a JSON file to programmatically configure Tailscale Serve and Tailscale Funnel' — consistent with Serve working in userspace mode, but no page states it outright. Treat 'Serve works on the userspace-mode hub' as UNVERIFIED until S-05 runs on solarplexus (or it is switched to kernel mode first).

tailscale/caddy-tailscale (Apache-2.0; repo description 'A highly experimental exploration of integrating Tailscale and Caddy'; status badge experimental; no release tags; last push 2026-01-06) embeds a tsnet node in Caddy and offers a listener, proxy transport, and an auth provider. Its README says 'you don't necessarily need this plugin to use Caddy with Tailscale. With Tailscale installed on a machine, Caddy can already bind to the Tailscale network interface, proxy requests to other Tailnet nodes, get automatic certificates, and authenticate Tailscale users' (linking Caddy's forward_auth Tailscale example). Requires a custom xcaddy build. Not recommended for CORVID.
facts.version: main branch, last push 2026-01-06 (no tags); LICENSE at main

facts.statement: `tailscale nginx-auth` (cmd/nginx-auth in the tailscale repo, BSD-3-Clause, status experimental) answers an auth sub-request over a unix socket (/run/tailscale.nginx-auth.sock, systemd socket activation) given `Remote-Addr` and `Remote-Port` headers, and returns `Tailscale-User` (user@host form), `Tailscale-Login`, `Tailscale-Name`, `Tailscale-Profile-Picture`, `Tailscale-Tailnet` for the proxy to copy into X-Webauth-* headers. It is the reference design for 'whois-as-forward_auth'; whether Ubuntu packages it (tailscale-nginx-auth) was not verified.
facts.version: tailscale v1.102.3; repo LICENSE BSD-3-Clause at tag

facts.statement: Beszel v0.18.8 (MIT, 2026-08-17) is 'a lightweight server monitoring platform' with a PocketBase hub + per-host agent; metrics include CPU, memory, disk, disk I/O, network, load, temperature, fan, 'GPU usage / power draw - Nvidia, AMD, and Intel', battery, Docker/Podman containers, S.M.A.R.T.; multi-user with OAuth/OIDC and password auth that can be disabled; agent connects outbound to the hub (HUB_URL + TOKEN + KEY); hub default port 8090 (collides with ADR-0003's inference port if co-hosted). It duplicates the CORVID agent's reporting rather than reading CORVID's Postgres — a reference design, not a component.
facts.version: beszel v0.18.8; LICENSE at tag; getting-started https://beszel.dev/guide/getting-started

facts.statement: Gatus v5.36.0 (Apache-2.0, 2026-05-19) is 'a developer-oriented health dashboard' monitoring HTTP/ICMP/TCP/DNS with conditions (status, response time, body, cert expiry) and alerting; 'External Endpoints' 'are not monitored by Gatus, but they are instead pushed programmatically' ('You can create your own agent that lives in a private network and pushes the status'); storage.type memory|sqlite|postgres. A plausible zero-code service-status page for llama-server/coordinator health checks, but it has no notion of capacity/utilisation/threshold panels.
Uptime Kuma 2.5.3 (MIT, 2026-08-22) is 'an easy-to-use self-hosted monitoring tool' (Node.js) — uptime/status-page class, not a metrics dashboard.

Perses v0.54.0 (Apache-2.0; CNCF sandbox; the Grafana-like 'dashboard as code' alternative) 'currently supports Prometheus metrics, Tempo traces, Loki for logs, Pyroscope for profiling' — no SQL/PostgreSQL data source, so it cannot read the CORVID roster directly.

Metabase v0.63.14: 'Outside of the top-level "enterprise" directory, source code in a given file is licensed under the AGPL'; the enterprise directory is under the Metabase Commercial License; hub.docker.com/metabase/metabase binaries are AGPL. A BI-over-Postgres option in the founder's stack, but like Grafana it brings its own login and is a second, heavier UI.

htmx LICENSE at v2.0.10 (latest 2.x tag; v4 is pre-release) is Zero-Clause BSD (0BSD) — an acceptable, tiny dependency if the server-rendered status page wants partial-page polling without a JS build step.

ADR-0001 (Accepted 2026-08-22) consequences: 'The dashboard shows pool capacity, utilisation, and how close the next product threshold is; contributions appear only as thanks'; no per-member quotas, counts or ranks; data hard-partitioned per member; identity comes from the mesh on every request; default posture no prompt/content logging anywhere.

Phase 2 acceptance (package design spec §7 + plan Task 28): all three build nodes live on the map with capabilities; node-down visible within N = 3 × the heartbeat interval chosen in R06 (plan sketches a 15 s heartbeat → N = 45 s); capability report carries only what the owner opted in (`offers`); status page v0 is 'a server-rendered page at :8092 or Grafana' with panels: node liveness map, pool capacity/utilisation, distance to next threshold, thank-you list — never counts/ranks; hub services are compose-bounded infrastructure; page shows a stale badge when Postgres is down; no prompt/content text in any log.

ADR-0003 (Proposed) and R00-F7: solarplexus ports 8090–8093 are free; ports 80 and 443 are not in the hub's listening list (free for Caddy/Serve); Caddy already runs on the hub on a custom port with path routes and its admin API on 2019; whether it is the Debian package (/etc/caddy/Caddyfile) or a container is not recorded in R00 — an open question for the Phase 2 plan.

recommendations: Status page v0 = a server-rendered page, not Grafana: FastAPI + Jinja2 (deps already chosen by R06 for the coordinator) serving `/status` at :8092, re-rendered every 5–15 s (meta refresh or htmx 0BSD polling). Rationale: ADR-0001's four panels are bespoke (threshold distance, thanks-without-numbers), the page must never offer a sortable per-member table, and Grafana adds AGPL, a second identity system, `0.0.0.0` and phone-home defaults (R07-F8) to a 16 GB hub shared with Plex/Immich. Keep Grafana as a Phase 4 option for time-series history; if adopted: image `grafana/grafana` (OSS, AGPL — not the proprietary enterprise image), GF_SERVER_HTTP_ADDR=127.0.0.1 (or tailnet IP), GF_ANALYTICS_REPORTING_ENABLED=false, GF_ANALYTICS_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=false, GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true org_role Viewer, GF_AUTH_DISABLE_LOGIN_FORM=true, optional [auth.proxy] fed by Caddy header_up from the identity header with whitelist=127.0.0.1, a SELECT-only Postgres role, dashboards provisioned as JSON from `deploy/grafana/`, and a §4 row (AGPL-3.0-only, Grafana Labs) in the same commit.

Live-map data contract (for R06's schema and the page): per node — name, owner display name, last_heartbeat_at, age = now() − last_heartbeat_at, state = live (age < 1×interval) / stale (< 3×) / down (≥ 3×), and only the opted-in capabilities (offers, cpu cores, ram_gb, gpu name + vram_mb, battery/idle flags) under the owner's slider caps. Pool capacity = Σ over live nodes of offered (capped) RAM/VRAM/cores; utilisation = currently assigned/used by CORVID work; thresholds = a small `product_threshold` table (product, metric, needed) so 'distance to next threshold' is `needed − current` rendered as a progress bar; thanks = alphabetical list of contributor names with no numbers, no order by amount, no per-member usage. No geo map of houses (privacy); the 'map' is logical. Page shows a 'stale data' badge when the last successful DB read is older than 2× the refresh.

Identity plumbing — decide by hub Tailscale mode and keep backends loopback-only: all CORVID backends (8090–8093) bind 127.0.0.1 on the hub; Caddy is the only tailnet-facing listener (`bind <tailnet IP>` in kernel mode; `bind 127.0.0.1` while solarplexus is in userspace mode, where tailscaled forwards inbound 100.x:80 → 127.0.0.1:80 — R07-F26). Preferred identity mechanism: a tiny CORVID `whoami` forward_auth endpoint (Python, ~30 lines) that runs `tailscale whois --json {remote_host}:{remote_port}` (or the LocalAPI whois over the unix socket) and returns Tailscale-User/Login/Name headers, wired exactly like Caddy's documented Tailscale forward_auth example (R07-F15, R07-F29). It works in both tailscaled modes, needs no HTTPS feature (no CT-log disclosure, R07-F19), and depends on nothing experimental. Alternative A: `tailscale serve --bg --http=80 http://127.0.0.1:<caddy>` (Serve injects headers and strips squatters, R07-F22/F23) — adopt only if S-05 shows headers on --http; Alternative B: Serve on https:443 (requires enabling HTTPS certs; accept CT-log exposure of `solarplexus.<tailnet>.ts.net`). In every variant Caddy must `header_up -Tailscale-User-Login` (and siblings) on the route *before* forward_auth/serve re-adds them, so a member cannot self-assert identity; and ADR-0002's ACL should expose only Caddy's port(s) to members, never 8090–8093.

ADR-0002 amendment: `tag:member` must not be applied to devices a member browses from — tagged nodes get no serve identity headers and whois returns tags, not a user (R07-F21/F22/F24). Tag hubs only; members' laptops/phones stay user-owned. If a member's contributing desktop is also their browsing device, leave it untagged and express the ACL in terms of users/autogroup:member instead.

Caddy integration on the hub: CORVID ships `deploy/caddy/corvid.caddy` (site block or snippet with `handle_path`/`handle` routes for /, /chat, /v1, /api, /status plus the forward_auth block) and the Phase 2 plan installs it via an `import` line in the existing Caddyfile (R07-F20), then `systemctl reload caddy` (or `docker exec caddy caddy reload` if the hub's Caddy is a container — open question). Use `handle /status/*` if the status app is mounted at /status, `handle_path` only for apps that expect to be at root (R07-F14). Leave the existing media-stack routes untouched. Access logs: default redaction is fine (R07-F17); never enable `log_credentials`; no request bodies are logged by Caddy.

S-05 scope (tighten the card): on ahnoway (kernel mode) and, once Phase 0 steps land, on solarplexus (userspace mode): (1) `tailscale serve --bg --http=8099 http://127.0.0.1:<echo>` — do identity headers appear? (2) `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 …` — same, and note whether the tailnet HTTPS prompt fires; (3) connect directly to 100.x:<echo> on the userspace hub and record the source IP/port the echo server sees; (4) `tailscale whois --json 127.0.0.1:<that port>` while the connection is open — does it resolve the peer? (5) repeat (3)/(4) after solarplexus is switched to kernel mode. Record exact header names and values (Login may be an email or `user@github`).

Lightweight alternatives — what they are good for: Gatus (Apache-2.0) as an optional zero-code *service* health page (HTTP checks of /v1/models, /api/health; external endpoints pushed by agents) if the founder wants uptime history without writing it; Beszel (MIT) only as a design reference for per-host metrics incl. NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPU (its hub port 8090 collides with ADR-0003 if co-hosted); Perses does not read SQL (skip); Uptime Kuma is uptime-only (skip); Metabase is a heavier AGPL BI UI (skip for v1). None replaces the ADR-0001 panels.

Log policy carried over from R06: the status page and whoami endpoint log only metadata (timestamp, path, status, latency, node id) — never identity header values in the access log beyond what Caddy logs by default, never query strings containing member names, never bodies.
open_questions: Hub Caddy: package or container? Where is its Caddyfile and which custom port does it listen on (R00 did not capture this)? Needed for the `import` drop-in and reload command.
Will solarplexus be switched from userspace to kernel mode before Phase 2 (status finding 10)? It decides bind strategy (tailnet IP vs 127.0.0.1) and whether whois needs ip:port.

S-05: do identity headers appear on `tailscale serve --http=<port>` (source says the Rewrite hook is shared, KB is silent)? Does Serve run at all on the userspace-mode hub at 1.98.4 / 1.102.3? What exact LoginName format do members get (email vs `user@github`)?

Is the tailnet HTTPS-certificates feature acceptable given CT-log publication of `<machine>.tail2990fc.ts.net` names (R07-F19)? If not, Serve-over-HTTPS and Caddy automatic *.ts.net certs are off the table and the front door stays plain HTTP on the mesh.
Is `tailscale nginx-auth` packaged for Ubuntu 24.04 (tailscale-nginx-auth)? (Only matters if the team prefers it over a CORVID whoami endpoint.)
Heartbeat interval (R06): 15 s → node-down at 45 s? The status page's stale/down colours depend on it.
If Grafana is adopted later: measure its RAM/CPU on the 16 GB hub next to Plex/Immich before committing; confirm the OSS image tag to pin (v13.2.0 today).
Member device tagging in ADR-0002's ACL baseline vs identity headers — needs a decision before the first member's device is tagged.

The page's [auth.proxy] example block reads verbatim: enabled = true; header_name = X-WEBAUTH-USER; header_property = username with comment "defaults to `username` but can also be `email`" (matches claim's username|email); auto_sign_up = true with comment "enable auto sign up of users who do not exist in Grafana DB. Depending on your filesystem and how you mount or sync dashboard files (for example, Docker bind mounts or some network filesystems), those events might not reach Grafana" — set >10 to force polling in a Docker deployment.

It sets the X-Forwarded-Proto header field. It sets the X-Forwarded-Host header field."; the exact sentence "For these X-Forwarded-* headers, by default, the proxy will ignore their values from incoming requests, to prevent spoofing."; "It is strongly recommended that you configure this via the servers > trusted_proxies global option instead of in the proxy" (a per-proxy trusted_proxies subdirective also exists, which the claim's parenthetical does not contradict); syntax lines "header_up   [+|-]<field> [<value|regexp> [<replacement>]]" and "header_down [+|-]<field> [<value|regexp> [<replacement>]]"; the example "header_up -Some-Header" under header deletion; upstream examples "localhost:4000", "http://localhost:4000", "h2c://127.0.0.1", "unix//var/php.sock"; and flush_interval listed under the "# streaming" block and described as adjusting how often Caddy flushes the response buffer to the client (negative value = low-latency mode). Fetched the cited primary source (official Caddy v2 docs, handle_path directive) on 2026-08-22. Verbatim text confirms the quote exactly: "Works the same as the handle directive, but implicitly uses uri strip_prefix to strip the matched path prefix." The page shows `handle_path /prefix/* {...}` "is effectively the same as" `handle /prefix/* { uri strip_prefix /prefix ... }`, and the full example contains `handle_path /api/* { reverse_proxy localhost:9000 }` commented "# Serve your API, stripping the /api prefix". The companion handle directive page confirms plain `handle` preserves the full request path ("handle_path does the same as handle, but it strips a prefix from the request before"). So the inference — handle_path /status/* when the app expects to sit at root, handle /status/* when the app knows its own prefix — is supported. Two caveats worth carrying into ADR-0003 (not refutations): (1) the docs page itself warns "be aware of the subfolder problem" — an app mounted at root that emits absolute links (/css/..., /api/...) will break behind a stripped prefix unless it supports a base-path setting; (2) the path matcher `/status/*` does not match bare `/status` (no trailing slash), so the ADR's `/status` → `:8092` needs either `/status*`-style matching or a `redir /status /status/` alongside the handle block. Source is primary and current for the stated version.

Fetched https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/forward_auth (official Caddy v2 docs, primary source, live on 2026-08-22). Every quoted phrase appears verbatim: "An opinionated directive which proxies a clone of the request to an authentication gateway"; "If the upstream responds with a 2xx status code, then access is granted and the header fields in copy_headers are copied to the original request, and handling continues. Otherwise, if the upstream responds with any other status code, then the upstream's response is copied back to the client"; "copy_headers is a list of HTTP header fields to copy from the response to the original request, when the request has a success status code. The field can be renamed by using > followed by the new name, for example Before>After." The "sugar over reverse_proxy" characterization is a fair paraphrase of the page's own wording ("opinionated wrapper over a reverse proxy", "a convenient way to use a longer, more common configuration", "the forward_auth shortcut"; "All the subdirectives of reverse_proxy are supported, and passed through to the underlying reverse_proxy handler"). The Tailscale example matches exactly: `forward_auth unix//run/tailscale.nginx-auth.sock { uri /auth; header_up Remote-Addr {remote_host}; header_up Remote-Port {remote_port}; header_up Original-URI {uri}; copy_headers { Tailscale-User>X-Webauth-User; Tailscale-Name>X-Webauth-Name; Tailscale-Login>X-Webauth-Login; Tailscale-Tailnet>X-Webauth-Tailnet; Tailscale-Profile-Picture>X-Webauth-Profile-Picture } }`, introduced with "Delegating authentication to Tailscale (currently named nginx-auth, but it still works with Caddy)". Every quoted element is verbatim on the primary source: "Overrides the interface to which the server's socket should bind."; "Normally, the listener binds to the empty (wildcard) interface."; "This directive accepts only a host, not a port." and "`bind` accepts network addresses, but may not include a port."; syntax block "bind <hosts...>" with "<hosts...> is the list of host interfaces to bind which to bind the listener."; examples "bind 127.0.0.1", "bind 127.0.0.1 [::1]", "bind 10.0.0.1" (under example.com:8080); and the parenthetical "(Virtual hosts are not shared across different listeners.)". The doc is the official Caddy v2 Caddyfile reference, so the source is primary and current for the stated version. The trailing sentence mapping bind to CLAUDE.md §5.6 (tailnet IP in kernel mode, 127.0.0.1 in userspace mode) is the dossier's own application, not a sourced fact, but it is consistent with the directive's documented behavior (binding a specific host instead of the wildcard interface). Minor note only: bind also accepts unix sockets (e.g. "bind unix//run/caddy"), so "addresses, no port" is an accurate paraphrase of "network addresses ... may not include a port".

Fetched https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/log (official Caddy v2 docs, primary source) on 2026-08-22 via both WebFetch and raw curl. The page opens verbatim with "Enables and configures HTTP request logging (also known as access logs)." and states verbatim "By default, headers with potentially sensitive information (Cookie, Set-Cookie, Authorization and Proxy-Authorization) will be logged as REDACTED in access logs. This behaviour can be disabled with the log_credentials global server option." Cross-checked https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/options which documents log_credentials identically. The log directive's syntax block documents only hostnames, no_hostname, output, format, level, and sampling (plus output modules stderr/stdout/discard/file/net and format modules console/json/filter/append); grepping the article HTML for body/payload/bodies yields no hit in the directive content — the sole "request_body" string on the page is a sidebar navigation link to the separate request_body directive (a size-limit directive, not a logging option). The claim is accurate for the stated version; not refuted.

Both primary sources fetched 2026-08-22 and support the claim verbatim. Caddy docs (https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https, "Special cases" under Activation) read: "Domains ending in .ts.net will not be managed by Caddy. Instead, Caddy will automatically attempt to get these certificates at handshake-time from the locally-running Tailscale instance. This requires that HTTPS is enabled in your Tailscale account and the Caddy process must either be running as root, or you must configure tailscaled to give your Caddy user permission to fetch certificates." Tailscale KB 1190 shows "Last validated: Jan 5, 2026" and reads: "Starting with the beta release of Caddy 2.5, Caddy supports Tailscale. When Caddy gets an HTTPS request for a *.ts.net site, it gets the HTTPS certificate from the machine's local Tailscale daemon. There's no configuration required for the certificate. For example, you can use a Caddyfile for a static file server, and it automatically enables HTTPS: machine-name.domain-alias.ts.net / root * /var/www / file_server" and "If Caddy is running as a non-root user, such as when it runs on Debian as caddy, you need to modify /etc/default/tailscaled ... set the TS_PERMIT_CERT_UID environment variable to the name or ID of the non-root user: TS_PERMIT_CERT_UID=caddy". Every quoted phrase, the validation date, the env var, the file path, and the site-block example match the claim exactly; no staleness found as of today.

Fetched https://tailscale.com/kb/1153/enabling-https (Tailscale's own KB, primary source; page header reads "Last validated: Dec 10, 2025", matching the stated version). Every element of the claim is supported verbatim or near-verbatim: (1) under "Configure HTTPS" the prerequisites list includes "Enable MagicDNS if not already enabled for your tailnet"; (2) "Using tailscale cert (with sudo as needed), Tailscale will automatically request a certificate for this machine on this domain, using Let's Encrypt" (DNS-01 challenge via a *.ts.net TXT record); (3) "The certificates provided by Let's Encrypt have a 90 day expiry and require periodic renewal... for any certificates that you create using tailscale cert, you are responsible for renewing the certificate. If a certificate is handled without the user initiating any file-based certificate installation, such as when using the Caddy integration of Tailscale, then the certificate will automatically be renewed without the user doing anything"; (4) "All TLS certificates on the web are recorded in the Certificate Transparency (CT) append-only public ledger... Do not enable the HTTPS feature if any of your machine names contain sensitive information." (exact sentence present), with names of the form machine-name.tailNNNN.ts.net / monitoring.yak-bebop.ts.net (machine name + tailnet DNS name); (5) "It is possible to frequently request a new certificate and exceed Let's Encrypt's rate limits. As a result, you may find yourself waiting 34 hours until you can try again." Only trivial nit: the page title is "Enabling HTTPS" (nav label "Set up HTTPS certificates"), not literally "HTTPS certificates KB" — not a substantive discrepancy. Claim stands.

Fetched both cited pages (2026-08-22). docs/running supports, near-verbatim: the recommended unit is caddy.service "if you configure Caddy with a Caddyfile"; you edit "sudo nano /etc/caddy/Caddyfile"; "If using a config file, you can gracefully reload Caddy after making any changes: sudo systemctl reload caddy" (and "Do not stop the service to change Caddy's configuration"); "The Caddy process will run as the caddy user" after "groupadd --system caddy" / "useradd --system --gid caddy ... caddy". The linked official unit (github.com/caddyserver/dist/blob/master/init/caddy.service) confirms User=caddy, Group=caddy, ExecStart=/usr/bin/caddy run --environ --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, ExecReload=/usr/bin/caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --force. The import page supports verbatim: "Includes a snippet or file, replacing this directive with the contents of the snippet or file"; "it is evaluated before the structure is parsed, and it can appear anywhere in the Caddyfile"; example "import sites-enabled/*"; and its examples use import inside site blocks (example.com { import cors example.com }). ONE GAP: docs/running never mentions the admin API or localhost:2019. That sub-claim is true but needs other primary sources: the command-line docs say of caddy reload "Because this command uses the API, the admin endpoint must not be disabled" and docs/api says "Default address: localhost:2019". Caveats the dossier should carry: (1) 2019 is the DEFAULT admin address - it can be changed or disabled via the `admin` global option, and if disabled `systemctl reload caddy` fails; (2) "instead of editing the hub's existing Caddyfile" is slightly overstated - the caddy-dist default Caddyfile has no import line, so the hub Caddyfile needs a one-time `import <dir>/*` line (unless it already has one), after which CORVID owns only its drop-in file; the glob is "always relative to the file the import appears in", "an empty glob pattern is not an error", and hidden files are skipped. Not refuted, but the citation for the admin-API detail should be docs/command-line + docs/api, and the wording tightened as below.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Caddy Linux service: the official caddy.service unit runs as User=caddy/Group=caddy, starts with `caddy run --environ --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile`, and ExecReload runs `caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --force`; config is applied with `sudo systemctl reload caddy`. `caddy reload` uses the admin API ("the admin endpoint must not be disabled"), whose default address is localhost:2019 (configurable/disable-able via the `admin` global option). The `import` directive "includes a snippet or file", accepts globs (`import sites-enabled/*`; paths relative to the importing file; empty glob is not an error; hidden files skipped) and "can appear anywhere in the Caddyfile" including inside site blocks — so after a one-time `import` line in the hub's Caddyfile (the shipped default Caddyfile has none), CORVID can own a drop-in route file.

research.dossier:
R08 — Chat front-end for Phase 1 (verified 2026-08-22, primary sources only)

SUMMARY VERDICT
- Phase 1 demo ("a friend gets a completion from a model spread across two houses"): llama-server's built-in Web UI is sufficient and costs zero extra services. It is MIT, ships inside the llama-server binary, stores each person's conversations in their own browser (IndexedDB), and has no login at all. It is single-user-by-design: no server-side per-user history, no identity. Bind llama-server to the tailnet interface (its default is 127.0.0.1:8080) and friends open http://solarplexus:8080.
- First member-facing chat (Phase 2 "bookmark the site"): Open WebUI v0.11.0 is the only candidate that satisfies all four asks at once — (a) zero-login via trusted headers (WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER / _NAME_HEADER), with an official Tailscale Serve tutorial (Serve injects Tailscale-User-Login / Tailscale-User-Name); (b) per-user chat history (SQLite, one container, default DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///{DATA_DIR}/webui.db); (c) telemetry already off in the official image (SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS=true, DO_NOT_TRACK=true, ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false; ENABLE_OTEL default False) with ENABLE_VERSION_UPDATE_CHECK / ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING / OFFLINE_MODE knobs; (d) single compose service. Licence caveat: since ~v0.6 it is NOT MIT — it is the "Open WebUI License", BSD-3-Clause plus a clause-4 branding restriction that is waived for deployments with ≤50 end users in any rolling 30-day period (CORVID qualifies; we would not rebrand anyway). Privacy caveat: ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS defaults True (admins can read every user's chats) — set False or disclose per §5.7.
- LibreChat v0.8.7 (MIT): no trusted-header auth exists in a release — the feature is an open, unmerged PR (#8562, opened 2025-07-20; issue #1856 still open). Its compose needs MongoDB (+ rag_api by depends_on) — not a single service. OIDC is supported, so a future zero-login path is Tailscale's tsidp (experimental). Defer.
- Lobe Chat (repo now lobehub/lobehub, v2.2.14): "LobeHub Community License" (Apache 2.0 + extra conditions: derivative works need a commercial licence; producer may tighten terms). Auth is Better Auth (email/password, OAuth/OIDC providers), sessions in the DB; no trusted-header mode documented; minimum three services (app + PostgreSQL/pgvector + S3/RustFS). Not a fit.
- Hollama 0.35.4 (MIT): runs entirely in the browser, no accounts, history per browser, one container (ghcr.io/fmaclen/hollama, port 4173), supports OpenAI-compatible servers, no analytics packages declared. A fine zero-backend alternative to the llama.cpp UI, but "per-user history" is just "per-browser".
- Also checked: AnythingLLM (MIT; multi-user Docker-only; telemetry ON by default, DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true to stop), Hugging Face chat-ui (Apache-2.0; MongoDB-backed, OPENAI_BASE_URL only). Neither documents header auth; neither beats Open WebUI for this use.

ZERO-LOGIN MECHANISM (verified): Tailscale Serve proxies to a local port and adds Tailscale-User-Login, Tailscale-User-Name, Tailscale-User-Profile-Pic; it strips those headers from incoming requests (anti-spoofing); headers are absent for Funnel traffic and for tagged devices; the backend must be reachable only via Serve (listen on localhost / publish the container port on 127.0.0.1). Tailscale Serve requires HTTPS certificates enabled on the tailnet. Alternative identity sources: `tailscale whois --json <ip>` (CLI) and tsidp (experimental OIDC IdP, BSD-3, ghcr.io/tailscale/tsidp).

RISK FLAGGED FOR THE HUB: solarplexus runs tailscaled with --tun=userspace-networking. Tailscale's userspace-networking and Serve docs do not state whether Serve works in that mode (neither yes nor no). This must be spiked before the Open WebUI + Serve design is committed; the Open WebUI tutorial's tailscale-sidecar compose pattern is the documented fallback.

facts.statement: Open WebUI's latest GitHub release is v0.11.0, published 2026-07-27T09:30:15Z.

The LICENSE file at tag v0.11.0 is titled "Open WebUI License", "Copyright (c) 2023- Open WebUI Inc. [Created by Timothy Jaeryang Baek]"; it follows BSD-3-Clause structure plus clause 4: licensees are "strictly prohibited from altering, removing, obscuring, or replacing any 'Open WebUI' branding" except (i) deployments where total end users do not exceed fifty (50) within any rolling thirty (30) day period, (ii) prior written permission, or (iii) an enterprise license; clause 5: prior materials keep their terms per LICENSE_HISTORY; contributors agree to a CLA. It is not MIT.

LICENSE_HISTORY at v0.11.0 states earlier code was MIT (materials created before commit a76068d69cd59568b920dfab85dc573dbbb8f131) and BSD-3-Clause (materials created before commit 60d84a3aae9802339705826e9095e272e3c83623); boundaries are given as commits, not version numbers.

Open WebUI supports trusted-header (reverse-proxy) authentication: WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER names the header whose value is used as the user's email, "handling automatic registration and login"; WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_NAME_HEADER sets the display name (email used if unset); WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_GROUPS_HEADER syncs comma-separated groups; WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER sets role. Warning: "Incorrect configuration can allow users to authenticate as any user... Make sure to allow only the authenticating proxy access to Open WebUI, such as by not opening any ports directly to the container, or by setting HOST=127.0.0.1". Docs list Tailscale Serve, Cloudflare Access, oauth2-proxy, Authentik, Authelia as supported proxies.

facts.statement: Open WebUI's official Tailscale tutorial: "When a request passes through `tailscale serve`, Tailscale automatically sets the `Tailscale-User-Login` header with the email address of the authenticated user"; set WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Login and WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_NAME_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Name; example `sudo tailscale serve https / http://localhost:8080`; it also shows a compose with a tailscale/tailscale sidecar + serve.json proxying to http://open-webui:8080. Caveat quoted: "If you run Tailscale in the same network context as Open WebUI, users could bypass the Serve proxy and reach Open WebUI directly, skipping the trusted header authentication."

Open WebUI hardening guide: "When using trusted headers, your proxy must strip these headers from incoming client requests before injecting its own values. If the proxy does not strip them, any client can send a forged header and authenticate as any user." Also: "Signup is open only until the first user registers, who becomes the administrator. After that, signup is automatically disabled." OFFLINE_MODE "disables HuggingFace Hub downloads, version update checks, and other outbound calls".

Per-user history isolation in Open WebUI is qualified by admin access: ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS (default True) "Controls whether the admin-panel other-users-chats access surface is available" (admins can view all user chats) and ENABLE_ADMIN_EXPORT (default True) controls admin export of data/chats/database. DEFAULT_USER_ROLE defaults to `pending` (new users need admin approval); ENABLE_SIGNUP defaults True.

llama-server (v0.2.0) ships a built-in Web UI: `--ui, --webui, --no-ui, --no-webui` "whether to enable the Web UI (default: enabled)"; "You can visit the web front end at the same url"; `--path PATH` serves custom static files; defaults --host 127.0.0.1, --port 8080; `--api-key KEY` (comma-separated list) / `--api-key-file`; `--rpc SERVERS` comma-separated RPC servers; OpenAI-compatible endpoints include GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/responses; --metrics default disabled; --slots default enabled.

The llama-server Web UI (source in tools/ui/ at v0.2.0; SvelteKit) is compiled into the llama-server binary and served at the root path; it stores "IndexedDB: Conversations and messages" (via Dexie) and "LocalStorage: Settings, user parameter overrides, theme" — all client-side; the README documents no authentication, accounts, or multi-user support.

Tailscale Serve adds identity headers to proxied requests: Tailscale-User-Login (e.g. alice@example.com), Tailscale-User-Name, Tailscale-User-Profile-Pic; "If Serve finds the following headers on an incoming request, it will remove them for security reasons, to avoid header spoofing"; "These identity headers are not populated for traffic originating from tagged devices"; Funnel traffic does not include identity headers; best practice: "only have the service listen on localhost"; "Tailscale Serve requires you to enable HTTPS certificates in your tailnet"; basic command `tailscale serve 3000` (HTTP variant: `tailscale serve --http=80 localhost:3000`).

tsidp is Tailscale's OIDC/OAuth identity provider for a tailnet: "tsidp is an experimental project. It is under active development and might experience breaking changes"; identity comes from LocalAPI whois; supports Dynamic Client Registration; runs as ghcr.io/tailscale/tsidp:latest with persistent TS_STATE_DIR; LICENSE is BSD 3-Clause, "Copyright (c) 2025 Tailscale Inc & AUTHORS".

`tailscale whois <ip>` returns "the machine and user associated with a Tailscale IP" and `--json` gives machine-readable output — usable by a CORVID-side proxy/agent to map a connecting tailnet IP to a member without any login.

Tailscale Serve (and therefore identity-header injection) works when tailscaled runs with --tun=userspace-networking, as on solarplexus — NOT confirmed either way: the userspace-networking page documents only SOCKS5/HTTP outbound proxies and the Serve pages make no statement about userspace mode. Must be spiked on the hub.

AnythingLLM is MIT ("Copyright (c) Mintplex Labs Inc."); README: "Multi-user instance support and permissioning Docker version only"; supports "Generic OpenAI" and llama.cpp-compatible providers; telemetry is on by default and disabled with DISABLE_TELEMETRY="true" (or the in-app Privacy sidebar). No trusted-header auth is documented in the README.

Hugging Face chat-ui is Apache License 2.0 ("Copyright 2018- The Hugging Face team"); "Chat UI only supports OpenAI-compatible APIs via OPENAI_BASE_URL"; "Chat history, users, settings, files, and stats all live in MongoDB" (embedded MongoDB fallback when MONGODB_URL unset; `chat-ui-db` image bundles it); README documents no OIDC/header auth.

recommendations: Phase 1 exit demo: use llama-server's built-in Web UI (MIT, inside the binary) — no extra service. Start llama-server with --host <solarplexus tailnet IP> (default is 127.0.0.1) and --rpc <workers>; friends open http://solarplexus:8080. Accept that history is per-browser and there is no identity; do not set --api-key for the demo (the UI is open to the tailnet, which is the security boundary per CLAUDE.md §3.2).

Member-facing chat (Phase 2 'bookmark the site'): adopt Open WebUI, pinned to a vX.Y.Z tag (v0.11.0 today; verify the GHCR tag exists — R08-F12), one container, SQLite on the open-webui volume, published on 127.0.0.1:8080 only, fronted by `tailscale serve` on solarplexus. Env: WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Login, WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_NAME_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Name, DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=user (else friends land 'pending'), OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://<llama-server>:8080/v1 with a dummy OPENAI_API_KEY, ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false, ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING=false, ENABLE_VERSION_UPDATE_CHECK=false (or OFFLINE_MODE=true if RAG downloads are not wanted), ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS=false and ENABLE_ADMIN_EXPORT=false (or disclose per §5.7 that the admin can read chats).

Record Open WebUI in CLAUDE.md §4 as 'Open WebUI License (BSD-3-Clause + branding clause)', not MIT; note CORVID's ≤50-end-users exemption (clause 4(i)) and the house rule: never rebrand it. Write ADR 'chat front-end' capturing this choice and the rejected options (LibreChat: no header auth in any release, MongoDB+rag_api; Lobe: custom licence + 3-service minimum + no header auth).

Before committing to the Serve design, run a spike on solarplexus: does `tailscale serve` work under --tun=userspace-networking and do the Tailscale-User-* headers arrive at a local listener (curl a tiny echo server)? If not, use the Open WebUI tutorial's tailscale-sidecar compose pattern (tailscale/tailscale container + serve.json -> http://open-webui:8080) or a tiny Python proxy that calls `tailscale whois --json` and injects the header itself.

Header-spoofing guard as a CI/ops check (ties to §5.6): the Open WebUI container must never be published on 0.0.0.0; only the Serve path may reach it. Tailscale Serve strips incoming Tailscale-User-* headers, but only if every request really goes through Serve.

Shared/tagged-device caveat: identity headers are not populated for tagged devices; design member nodes as user-owned (untagged) devices, and test what header value a member who logged into Tailscale with GitHub (non-email login) produces before relying on it as an 'email'.

Keep Hollama (MIT, one container, browser-local data) as the documented zero-backend fallback if Open WebUI ever feels heavy; keep LibreChat on the watch list keyed to PR #8562 merging or tsidp leaving 'experimental' (OIDC path). Do not adopt Lobe Chat.

Telemetry statement for members: Open WebUI's official image already ships SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS=true, DO_NOT_TRACK=true, ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false, ENABLE_OTEL off; what remains outbound is the version check (disable) and any HF model downloads for RAG/STT (document or set OFFLINE_MODE).
open_questions: Does Tailscale Serve run (and inject identity headers) on solarplexus's userspace-networking tailscaled? Not documented either way (R08-F34) — spike required; fallback is the tailscale sidecar container pattern from Open WebUI's tutorial.
Does the GHCR image tag ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.11.0 (and -slim/-cuda variants) exist, and which exact tag/digest do we pin? (R08-F12)

With trusted-header auth on, does Open WebUI still auto-create accounts when ENABLE_SIGNUP=false, and does DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=user apply to header-created users? The docs describe auto-registration but not this interplay.
What does Tailscale-User-Login contain for members who sign in to Tailscale via GitHub or other non-email identities, and is that value acceptable to Open WebUI's email-based identity? Untested.

Shared nodes (per memory, Zach's machine is a shared node) and tagged devices: do identity headers arrive for requests originating from a device shared from another tailnet? Docs only say tagged devices get no headers.
Privacy policy decision for the member page (§5.7): do we set ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS=false, or keep it true and disclose that the founder can read chats? Needs an explicit decision in the ADR.
LibreChat: will PR #8562 (reverse-proxy auth headers) merge, and does tsidp leave 'experimental' — triggers for re-evaluating LibreChat (MIT) as a richer front-end?

Open WebUI RAG/STT features pull models from Hugging Face at first use unless OFFLINE_MODE/HF_HUB_OFFLINE is set — decide whether Phase 2 wants those features at all (they also grow the image and data volume).

Tailscale free-plan seat count vs. the number of friends who need zero-login identity (CLAUDE.md §3.1 says 6 users as of mid-2026 — re-verify on the pricing page before the ADR; not checked in this dossier).

research.dossier:
R09 — SharedLLM & alternatives (verified 2026-08-22, primary sources only)

HEADLINE
None of the five candidates coordinates stock llama.cpp RPC workers across a Linux+macOS+Windows fleet today. The one that did (SharedLLM) has taken its source private and pivoted to a closed macOS desktop node that auto-joins a public global fleet; GPUStack dropped llama.cpp/llama-box and macOS/Windows workers in v2.0.0; exo 1.x is MLX-only (macOS GPU, Linux CPU, no Windows) and has gone quiet; prima.cpp is a research fork of llama.cpp with its own ring parallelism, no releases, no Windows; Ollama is single-host by design. CORVID's plan to keep a small Python+Postgres coordinator of its own around llama.cpp RPC stands — and CLAUDE.md §3.2's "Phase 5 mandate: evaluate adopting/contributing to SharedLLM" needs an ADR, because there is nothing public to adopt or contribute to.

SHAREDLLM (sharedllm.org; source repo MHASK/sharedllm — now private)
- What it was: v0.1.0 "public alpha" announced 2026-04-11 — Python coordinator + node daemon (sharedllm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl) wrapping stock llama.cpp rpc-server/llama-server binaries (shipped for macOS arm64/Metal, Linux x86_64, Linux arm64, Windows x86_64), HMAC-SHA256 cluster secret, worker discovery, free-memory tracking, split planning, re-planning on node drop. Its own words: only the tiny stories260K model verified end-to-end; larger quants hit an upstream RPC assertion; "If you need a production-grade mesh today, SharedLLM is not that project."
- What it is now: github.com/MHASK/sharedllm returns 404 (web and API). The only public artifact is MHASK/sharedllm-releases, whose README says "Source code lives in the private MHASK/sharedllm repo. This repo holds binaries only." Releases v0.1.0 (2026-06-08), v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 (2026-06-10) are macOS Apple Silicon .dmg only; v0.2.0 notes: zero-config, "the app joins the sharedllm.org fleet on first launch", RAM/disk capped at 2 GB. sharedllm.org footer: "An open-source initiative from Naridon, Inc. ... License: AGPLv3 | Source Code on GitHub", "Currently in beta with live nodes." The AGPL-3.0-or-later claim cannot be verified against any LICENSE file at any tag. No PyPI package (pypi.org/pypi/sharedllm → 404).
- Verdict for CORVID: not adoptable, not contributable, and its current direction (closed node, public global fleet, auto-join) conflicts with §1/§5/§7 (friends-only, opt-in, zero public exposure). Keep it as *prior art for design ideas* (HMAC-authenticated RPC proxy, free-memory tracking, re-plan on drop) credited to its blog posts, and record the pivot in an ADR. (Aside: its April-2026 comparison table lists exo as GPL-3.0/tinygrad — stale; see exo.)

EXO (exo-explore/exo)
- Latest release v1.0.71, 2026-04-23; no newer release or prerelease. LICENSE at v1.0.71: Apache-2.0, "Copyright 2025 Exo Technologies Ltd". The repo was GPL-3.0 from 2024-07-16 through at least v0.0.15-alpha (2025-02-25); the licence changed during "prep repo for v1" (2025-12-17/18).
- Matrix at v1.0.71: MLX backend + MLX distributed; macOS uses the GPU (app requires macOS Tahoe 26.2+; RDMA over Thunderbolt 5); "Currently, exo runs on CPU on Linux. GPU support for Linux platforms is under development." No mention of Windows, CUDA, NVIDIA, AMD or llama.cpp anywhere in the README. Own sharding: auto-discovery, tensor parallelism (claimed 1.8x/3.2x on 2/4 devices), topology-aware auto parallel, MlxRing pipeline.
- Linux CUDA: tracking issue #913 open since 2025-12-18 (last update 2026-02-02). The pre-1.0 tinygrad engine that gave Linux/NVIDIA support was dropped in the v1 rewrite. Scottcjn/exo-cuda is an independent GPL-3.0 repo ("CUDA support via tinygrad", Linux only, CUDA 12.0+/driver 525+, v1.0.0 2026-01-02, 92 stars, still pushed 2026-08-20) descended from the GPL-era code — it is not a CUDA port of exo 1.x, and its licence differs from upstream's.
- Maturity: 46,960 stars; last commit 2026-06-22; issue #2258 "Is this repository even actively being watched and maintained…" (2026-08-03) open with 13 comments and no maintainer reply visible.
- Verdict: Mac-only experiment at best (Apple-Silicon friends), as CLAUDE.md already says; §3.2's sentence about the CUDA fork should be corrected (GPL-3.0, tinygrad, pre-1.0 lineage).

GPUSTACK (gpustack/gpustack)
- Latest v2.2.3, 2026-07-31 (2026 cadence: 2.1.0 Mar-07 … 2.2.0 Jun-18, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3). LICENSE at v2.2.3: Apache-2.0, "Copyright (c) 2024 The GPUStack authors". Very active (last commit 2026-08-21; ≥100 commits since 2026-05-01; 5,535 stars; 684 open issues).
- Matrix: README v2.2.3 — "Only Linux is supported for GPUStack worker nodes. If you use Windows, consider using WSL2 and avoid using Docker Desktop. macOS is not supported for GPUStack worker nodes." Docs 2.2 (=latest): Linux AMD64/ARM64 only; NVIDIA needs a driver supporting CUDA 12.8+ plus NVIDIA Container Toolkit (solarplexus at driver 535/CUDA 12.2 fails this); AMD ROCm 7.0+; plus Ascend/Hygon/MThreads/Iluvatar/MetaX/Cambricon/T-Head.
- llama.cpp: "llama-box is no longer supported as of v2.0.0. Use llama.cpp via the custom inference backend instead." and "Distributed inference across multiple workers is currently not supported with custom inference backends." Built-in backends are vLLM, SGLang, MindIE, VoxBox; cross-worker distribution is "(Experimental)" via Ray sidecar or vLLM multiprocessing, Linux-only nodes. So GPUStack neither coordinates llama.cpp RPC nor runs on our Mac/Windows members.
- Verdict: off the v1 candidate list; keep only as a pattern source (cluster UI, Prometheus/Grafana pairing).

PRIMA.CPP
- The seed URL github.com/Lizonghang/prima.cpp is dead (404; user Lizonghang also 404). The ICLR 2026 paper's arXiv v3 (2026-07-04) points to github.com/OpenCPIL/prima.cpp ("[Official] prima.cpp…"), an org repo created 2026-06-30 by "Initial import" — history reset; 8 commits all on 2026-06-30; 0 tags; 0 releases; 81 stars; one contributor (zonghang-li). MIT ("Copyright (c) 2023-2024 The ggml authors and 2024-2025 the prima.cpp authors."). facts.statement: SharedLLM v0.1.0 'public alpha' was announced 2026-04-11 as 'a community-owned AI compute mesh built on llama.cpp RPC'; the release comprised a Python coordinator + node daemon (sharedllm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl + sdist) and pre-built rpc-server/llama-server bundles for macOS Apple Silicon (Metal), Linux x86_64, Linux arm64 and Windows x86_64; coordinator/worker handshake uses an HMAC-SHA256 cluster secret.

SharedLLM's own description of its coordinator: it 'discovers workers, tracks each one's free memory, builds the split for you, re-plans when a machine drops, and wraps the raw RPC socket in an authenticated (HMAC-SHA256) proxy' around stock llama.cpp rpc-server and llama-server — i.e. it coordinates llama.cpp RPC workers rather than shipping its own sharding engine.

SharedLLM's own maturity statement at v0.1.0: 'Only the tiny stories260K test model is verified end-to-end cross-container; larger quantized models hit a known upstream llama.cpp RPC assertion on certain tensor shapes'; 'If you need a production-grade mesh today, SharedLLM is not that project.' Governance claimed: AGPL-3.0-or-later, DCO not CLA, non-profit.

The SharedLLM source repository linked from every sharedllm.org page, https://github.com/MHASK/sharedllm, returns HTTP 404 on github.com and via the GitHub REST API; a GitHub repository search for 'sharedllm' returns no public repository belonging to the project; pypi.org/pypi/sharedllm also returns 404.

verdicts.reason: Fetched the cited source (HTTP 200). It is the project's own announcement on sharedllm.org, authored by "SharedLLM contributors" (primary). Every element of the claim is present verbatim or near-verbatim: title "Announcing SharedLLM v0.1.0 — public alpha", datePublished 2026-04-11; JSON-LD description "First public alpha of SharedLLM, a community-owned AI compute mesh built on llama.cpp RPC." (body prose says "a global, community-owned AI compute mesh"); "What's in the release": rpc-binaries-darwin-arm64.tar.gz (macOS Apple Silicon, Metal + RPC), rpc-binaries-linux-arm64.tar.gz, rpc-binaries-linux-x86_64.tar.gz, rpc-binaries-windows-x86_64.zip, and "sharedllm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl + sdist — the Python coordinator and node daemon"; "Coordinator + worker handshake with HMAC-SHA256 cluster secret." The claim's gloss "rpc-server/llama-server bundles" is confirmed by the companion post on the same site (https://sharedllm.org/blog/llama-cpp-rpc-two-macs.html, same date): "The v0.1.0 public alpha ships pre-built rpc-server and llama-server binaries for macOS, Linux (x86_64 + arm64), and Windows". License stated as AGPL-3.0-or-later. Caveat for the dossier (not a refutation of the stated fact): the GitHub release page the post links to (github.com/MHASK/sharedllm/releases/tag/v0.1.0) and the source repo now return 404 — the source repo is private per the README of the new binaries-only repo github.com/MHASK/sharedllm-releases (created 2026-06-08: "Source code lives in the private MHASK/sharedllm repo"), whose "v0.1.0" (2026-06-08) / v0.2.0 / v0.2.1 (2026-06-10) releases are a macOS-aarch64-only desktop app (.dmg), not the wheel + four-platform rpc-binaries described in the April announcement; no sharedllm package exists on PyPI. So the claim is accurate as a description of the 2026-04-11 v0.1.0 announcement, but those artifacts are no longer publicly retrievable and the project's current public distribution differs materially.

Fetched the cited page directly (HTTP 200). It is primary (sharedllm.org, the project's own site; JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified = 2026-07-18, matching the stated version). It's the RPC backend you just set up, minus the babysitting, under AGPL-3.0 so it can't be fenced off later."
